1.s: athātaḥ prāyaścittāni | athātaḥ kramāṇāṃ vadaye gṛhastho vā brahmacārī vā gṛhastho gṛhāgnau brahmacārī laukikāgnau gṛhasyeṣviticaraṇena paricaraṇe vā brahmacaryavicchinne laukikāgnau prātarāhutipūrvakaṃ naimittikaṃ kāryaṃm | punarādhāne varjayet sāyamupakramya tātkālikaprāyaścittāpattau cettābhyāṃ tatra kāryam | paurṇamyāhutyāmatītaṃ cettābhyāṃ tattatkuryuḥ parvaṇā cetsaṃkalya kāryam tadabhāve sadyaḥ kuryād apareṇa darśaṃ tve prāyaścittiḥ trirātraṃ pañcarātraṃ vā dadharātrāttāḥ prāyaścittapūrvayajña yajete tāvubhau parvā saṃkalya tītau tāmiṣṭau tadvat tatra yadi lopaṃ vā taṃ māmāsādatītaṃ vā punarādhānaṃ kuryuḥ | prāyaścittārthe prājāpatyaṃ vā tadūrdhvaṃ viśeṣaśca gṛhāgnau gṛhyāgniṃ yadi sparśettaṃtra ta meko vā kāryo mantrāṇāṃ tāvubhau brūyāttaṃtrī tatsamidho saṃyuktaṃ gṛhṇan navarohaṇaṃ tataḥ karma prāṇāyāmaṃ kuryuḥ | tūṣṇīṃ pariṣicya mantreṇābhyarvyāhutyāmanartha staras tāvubho dvau samidhamādhāya bhaṣatkarmāṃ mantraṃ brūyāt | atra pupastūṣṇīṃ kāryaṃ patnī vā iti samānaṃ samāropaṇaṃ kuryuḥ kartavyā iti vaitadu bhavati svayaṃ svayaṃ prāyaścittī tata ūrdhvaṃ viśeṣaṃ syād anyāgno svayamamasmadbhāvi tathāci yajñidknevarohaṇaṃ kuryāṃ ādisamāropaṇaṃ prajñātastadamavrimutsṛjya bhūrbhuvaḥ svariti brūyāḥ | tūṣṇīṃ tiṣṭhan na gacchet tadagnipatyāṃ ta prāpnau karmabhraṣṭā svagṛhyāgnau svayaṃ svayaṃ prāyaścittir ata ūrdhvaṃ viśeṣaṃ syādājyatantrairanāropaṇaṃ cetsamāropaṇaṃ prājñātaḥ punarārabhya prāyarāhutyādi prapadāntaparyantaṃ yatkiṃcitkarma yadi lopaṃ syāt prātarāhutiścetprāyaścittamityeke nyūnākarmādi punarāvṛttiḥ pradhānādūrdhvaṃ prāyaścittir ata ūrdhvaṃ viśeṣaścarutantreṇa tato vyākhyātā prāgudakpravaṇe deśe tatra sthaṃḍisamupali yāt |
1.d: अथातः प्रायश्चित्तानि । अथातः क्रमाणां वदये गृहस्थो वा ब्रह्मचारी वा गृहस्थो गृहाग्नौ ब्रह्मचारी लौकिकाग्नौ गृहस्येष्वितिचरणेन परिचरणे वा ब्रह्मचर्यविच्छिन्ने लौकिकाग्नौ प्रातराहुतिपूर्वकं नैमित्तिकं कार्यंम् । पुनराधाने वर्जयेत् सायमुपक्रम्य तात्कालिकप्रायश्चित्तापत्तौ चेत्ताभ्यां तत्र कार्यम् । पौर्णम्याहुत्यामतीतं चेत्ताभ्यां तत्तत्कुर्युः पर्वणा चेत्संकल्य कार्यम् तदभावे सद्यः कुर्याद् अपरेण दर्शं त्वे प्रायश्चित्तिः त्रिरात्रं पञ्चरात्रं वा दधरात्रात्ताः प्रायश्चित्तपूर्वयज्ञ यजेते तावुभौ पर्वा संकल्य तीतौ तामिष्टौ तद्वत् तत्र यदि लोपं वा तं मामासादतीतं वा पुनराधानं कुर्युः । प्रायश्चित्तार्थे प्राजापत्यं वा तदूर्ध्वं विशेषश्च गृहाग्नौ गृह्याग्निं यदि स्पर्शेत्तंत्र त मेको वा कार्यो मन्त्राणां तावुभौ ब्रूयात्तंत्री तत्समिधो संयुक्तं गृह्णन् नवरोहणं ततः कर्म प्राणायामं कुर्युः । तूष्णीं परिषिच्य मन्त्रेणाभ्यर्व्याहुत्यामनर्थ स्तरस् तावुभो द्वौ समिधमाधाय भषत्कर्मां मन्त्रं ब्रूयात् । अत्र पुपस्तूष्णीं कार्यं पत्नी वा इति समानं समारोपणं कुर्युः कर्तव्या इति वैतदु भवति स्वयं स्वयं प्रायश्चित्ती तत ऊर्ध्वं विशेषं स्याद् अन्याग्नो स्वयममस्मद्भावि तथाचि यज्ञिद्क्नेवरोहणं कुर्यां आदिसमारोपणं प्रज्ञातस्तदमव्रिमुत्सृज्य भूर्भुवः स्वरिति ब्रूयाः । तूष्णीं तिष्ठन् न गच्छेत् तदग्निपत्यां त प्राप्नौ कर्मभ्रष्टा स्वगृह्याग्नौ स्वयं स्वयं प्रायश्चित्तिर् अत ऊर्ध्वं विशेषं स्यादाज्यतन्त्रैरनारोपणं चेत्समारोपणं प्राज्ञातः पुनरारभ्य प्रायराहुत्यादि प्रपदान्तपर्यन्तं यत्किंचित्कर्म यदि लोपं स्यात् प्रातराहुतिश्चेत्प्रायश्चित्तमित्येके न्यूनाकर्मादि पुनरावृत्तिः प्रधानादूर्ध्वं प्रायश्चित्तिर् अत ऊर्ध्वं विशेषश्चरुतन्त्रेण ततो व्याख्याता प्रागुदक्प्रवणे देशे तत्र स्थंडिसमुपलि यात् ।
1.m:
Now then, the expiations.
Now then, for the order of ceremonies: either a householder or a Vedic student; a householder in the domestic fire, a Vedic student in the common fire. In the householder's rituals, whether in serving [the fire] or when the studentship is broken, the occasional rite preceded by the morning oblation is to be performed in the common fire.
In the case of re-establishment of the fire, he should avoid [the fire of another]; beginning in the evening, if an expiation for the particular occasion is incurred, the rite is to be performed by both of them there.
If the oblation has lapsed on the full-moon day, they should perform those respective rites with both [oblations]; and if on a joint day, he should perform it having combined [them]; in the absence of that, he should perform it immediately; but on the subsequent new-moon day, there is an expiation. For three nights or five nights, or from midnight, those [oblations] preceded by an expiation sacrifice—both of them should sacrifice, having combined both joint days; when those two rites have lapsed, similarly in that case, if there is an omission or if it has lapsed beyond a month, they should perform the re-establishment of the fire.
For the sake of expiation, either a Prājāpatya penance [is performed]; and further there is a particular rule: if one touches the domestic fire in the house-fire, in that ritual either one is to be performed; he should recite both of the mantras; taking [the wood] connected with those kindling sticks, the ritual then is descent [of the fire]; they should perform breath-control.
Having sprinkled [water] silently, having worshipped with the mantra, upon the mystic utterance […] both of them, having laid on two kindling sticks, he should recite the mantra for the offering rite.
Here the cake is to be made silently, or the wife [does it]; thus equally they should perform the internalisation of the sacred fire. Or rather, it must be performed; he is individually one requiring expiation; beyond that, there should be a particular rule; if [the fire] is in another fire, it is to become our own; similarly, one should perform the descent of the sacrificial [fire]; the initial internalisation of the sacred fire is well known; having released that […], you should say: “Bhūr bhuvas svar”.
Standing silently, he should not go away; in that keeping of the fire […] having failed in the rite; in one’s own domestic fire, he is individually one requiring expiation; beyond this, there is a particular rule: if there is no internalisation according to the procedures of the clarified butter offerings, [then] the internalisation is well known; having begun again, whatever rite from the morning oblation up to the introductory formula might be omitted, if it is the morning oblation, some say there is an expiation; repetition of a deficient rite and the like; beyond the primary rite there is expiation; beyond this, the particular rule is explained next according to the ritual procedure for cooked mess; in a place sloping towards the north-east, there he should smear the sacrificial ground.

2.s: athātaḥ prāṅmukho bhūtvodagagreṣu darbheṣu omityuccairupaviśya gṛhāgnau nirīkṣyamāṇollekhanaṃ tataḥ kārayet | tatprātarāhutiṃ hutvā vedavidbrāhmaṇaṃ labhet tadalābhe khādiranyāyaḥ chatraguttarāsaṃ ceti khādiraṃ nyā ityeke brāhmaṇaṃ prārthayet | brāhmaṇaṃ bhūrbhuvaḥ svaḥ bṛhaspatirbrahmāhaṃ mānuṣa iti brūyāt ācāryo dve darbhāgna dadyāt brāhmaṇo nirastaḥ parāvasuriti dakṣiṇāstṛṇaṃ nirasyāsanārthe prāgagrāndarbhānāstīryā vasoḥ sadane sīdāmotyudaṅmukha omityupāṃśuruviśed ācāryo brāhmaṇamarcayitvā tataḥ kāṃsyapātramādāya mṛnmayapātraṃ vābhidyam tāmravarjaṃ rajata iti śālitaṇḍulānnavaśūrpeṇādāyodagudvāsyo nirvāpārthena sakṛtpātraṃ pūrayet | dvistūṣṇīṃ kāryamo prokṣyāmīti brūyād āpaḥ prāvayantyudagudvāsya tataḥ samūhanādyājyatantreṣu gṛhyokte navaparvaṇaṃ kāryaṃ tatpātnamutthāpyāgnimadhye sthāpyo nirvāpa iti brūyāt tadā jīvasaṇḍulān śrapayet | sruveṇābhighāryāgnerbahistaraṇādaṃtayorudagudvāsya punaḥ prokṣaṇaṃ kuryāt | tata idhmamādāya tatra viśeṣaḥ samidhamucyace | bahvacāḥ khādireṇa bodhāyanāḥ palāśeśchandogāḥ udajumbareṇa yajante | prādeśamātrāḥ kaśapṛṣṭhāḥ samāgratoguṃṣṭhaparvaghṛtadyumātroḥ prajñātāgrāḥ kārayitvā tadabhāve darbhairvā saptadaśaiḥ ādāya anaṣṭārthamekaṃ prapadārthamekamidhmārthe pacadaśam etāni saptadaśa gṛhṇan sruveṇābhighārya agramavyamūlonyanuyājārthamuttarato nidhāya paṃcadaśamagno prakṣipya śeṣeṇa prapadaṃ jape yāvacīriti śaṭhāntāni tāvatsvāṣaso dhārayanta rūpāhanagnau hutvā śeṣākṣatānabhyarcya tato vyāhṛtibhiḥ tisṛbhiḥ hutvā tato kāmajavyāhṛkī ca hutvā cakṣuṣī caturgṛhītaṃ sruveṇa juhuyāt | eteṣāṃ carutantre eteṣāṃ yathārthaṃ syāt tatra viśeṣastu varadānaprayogocyate | khādiranyāyena ca gṛhyokteḥ kuthumasya mathādityuktvā kauthumo kuthumasya mārgamācarati |
2.d: अथातः प्राङ्मुखो भूत्वोदगग्रेषु दर्भेषु ओमित्युच्चैरुपविश्य गृहाग्नौ निरीक्ष्यमाणोल्लेखनं ततः कारयेत् । तत्प्रातराहुतिं हुत्वा वेदविद्ब्राह्मणं लभेत् तदलाभे खादिरन्यायः छत्रगुत्तरासं चेति खादिरं न्या इत्येके ब्राह्मणं प्रार्थयेत् । ब्राह्मणं भूर्भुवः स्वः बृहस्पतिर्ब्रह्माहं मानुष इति ब्रूयात् आचार्यो द्वे दर्भाग्न दद्यात् ब्राह्मणो निरस्तः परावसुरिति दक्षिणास्तृणं निरस्यासनार्थे प्रागग्रान्दर्भानास्तीर्या वसोः सदने सीदामोत्युदङ्मुख ओमित्युपांशुरुविशेद् आचार्यो ब्राह्मणमर्चयित्वा ततः कांस्यपात्रमादाय मृन्मयपात्रं वाभिद्यम् ताम्रवर्जं रजत इति शालितण्डुलान्नवशूर्पेणादायोदगुद्वास्यो निर्वापार्थेन सकृत्पात्रं पूरयेत् । द्विस्तूष्णीं कार्यमो प्रोक्ष्यामीति ब्रूयाद् आपः प्रावयन्त्युदगुद्वास्य ततः समूहनाद्याज्यतन्त्रेषु गृह्योक्ते नवपर्वणं कार्यं तत्पात्नमुत्थाप्याग्निमध्ये स्थाप्यो निर्वाप इति ब्रूयात् तदा जीवसण्डुलान् श्रपयेत् । स्रुवेणाभिघार्याग्नेर्बहिस्तरणादंतयोरुदगुद्वास्य पुनः प्रोक्षणं कुर्यात् । तत इध्ममादाय तत्र विशेषः समिधमुच्यचे । बह्वचाः खादिरेण बोधायनाः पलाशेश्छन्दोगाः उदजुम्बरेण यजन्ते । प्रादेशमात्राः कशपृष्ठाः समाग्रतोगुंष्ठपर्वघृतद्युमात्रोः प्रज्ञाताग्राः कारयित्वा तदभावे दर्भैर्वा सप्तदशैः आदाय अनष्टार्थमेकं प्रपदार्थमेकमिध्मार्थे पचदशम् एतानि सप्तदश गृह्णन् स्रुवेणाभिघार्य अग्रमव्यमूलोन्यनुयाजार्थमुत्तरतो निधाय पंचदशमग्नो प्रक्षिप्य शेषेण प्रपदं जपे यावचीरिति शठान्तानि तावत्स्वाषसो धारयन्त रूपाहनग्नौ हुत्वा शेषाक्षतानभ्यर्च्य ततो व्याहृतिभिः तिसृभिः हुत्वा ततो कामजव्याहृकी च हुत्वा चक्षुषी चतुर्गृहीतं स्रुवेण जुहुयात् । एतेषां चरुतन्त्रे एतेषां यथार्थं स्यात् तत्र विशेषस्तु वरदानप्रयोगोच्यते । खादिरन्यायेन च गृह्योक्तेः कुथुमस्य मथादित्युक्त्वा कौथुमो कुथुमस्य मार्गमाचरति ।
2.m:
Now then, having faced east, having sat down upon darbha grass with points directed to the north loudly pronouncing ‘Om’, he should then have the drawing of the lines performed while looking into the domestic fire.
Having offered that morning oblation, he should obtain a brahmin priest who knows the Veda; in his absence, the rule of the Khādira school [applies]; having [said]: ‘A parasol and an upper garment’, that is the rule of the Khādira school—so say some—he should invite the brahmin priest.
He should say to the brahmin priest: ‘Bhūr bhuvas svar; Bṛhaspati is the Brahmā priest, I am the human one.’ The preceptor should give two blades of darbha grass. The brahmin priest, [reciting:] ‘Parāvasu is cast away’, having cast away a blade of grass to the south, having spread darbha grass with points directed east for a seat, [reciting:] ‘May I sit in the seat of the Vasu’, facing north, should sit down softly uttering ‘Om’. The preceptor, having worshipped the brahmin priest, then having taken a bronze vessel or an unbroken earthen vessel, excluding copper, [or] silver, having taken husked grains of rice with a new winnowing-basket, having moved it to the north, should fill the vessel once for the purpose of the ritual pouring out of sacrificial grain.
It is to be done twice silently. He should say: ‘I sprinkle [it] with Om.’ The waters clarify [it]; having moved it to the north, then, among the procedures of the clarified butter offerings beginning with sweeping up [the sacrificial ground] as stated in the domestic manual, the rite of the new-moon day is to be done; having lifted that vessel and placed it in the middle of the fire, he should say: ‘[This is] the ritual pouring out of sacrificial grain.’ Then he should cook the living grains of rice.
Having basted [it] with the sacrificial ladle, having moved it to the north of the two ends of the grass strewn around the fire, he should perform the consecration by sprinkling again.
Then, taking the sacrificial firewood, a particular rule regarding the kindling stick is stated there:
The Ṛgvedic priests sacrifice with khādira wood, the Baudhāyanas with palāśa, the Sāmavedic chanters with udumbara.
Having caused them to be made a span in length, with edges like a whip’s back, straight-tipped, of the measure of the thumb-joint [or] of the measure of an oblation of clarified butter, with well-marked tips—in their absence, with seventeen [blades] of darbha grass—having taken [them], taking these seventeen: one for the sake of what is not destroyed, one for the sake of the introductory formula, fifteen for the sake of the sacrificial firewood; having basted [them] with the sacrificial ladle, having placed the tip, the middle, and the root to the north for the sake of the after-offerings, having thrown the fifteen into the fire, he should mutter the introductory formula with the remainder; as long as […] ends in śaṭha, so long wearing good garments, having offered the forms into the fire, having worshipped the remaining unhusked grains, then having offered with the three mystic utterances, then having offered the mystic utterance of desire, he should offer the fourfold-taken [clarified butter] into the two eyes [of the fire] with the sacrificial ladle.
Among these, in the ritual procedure for cooked mess, these should be according to purpose; but the specific rule there is stated in the manual on the granting of boons.
And by the rule of the Khādira school, from what is stated in the domestic manual: ‘according to the opinion of Kuthuma’—having said this, the Kauthuma follower follows the path of Kuthuma.

3.s: athātaḥ carupātraṃ nirīkṣya saṃmukhe sthāpanaṃ kāryam udagugvāsya ityeke saṃmukhe kāryaḥ carordvibhāgaṃ kāryaṃ sruvapātramāsādya cchidvānārdaṃ tadabhāve kāṃsyapātraṃ vā tanmadhye 'bhighārya caroḥ pūrvadeśe sakṛdavadāya dvitīyye madhyame hyavadānaṃ śeṣe sruvapātre punaścābhidhārya agnimadhye juhuyāt tvadvitīyaṃ ceñcaroḥ paścimadeśe syātsakṛvadāya dvibhighāryā prāgudagdeśe juguyayāj jāmadagnyāścenmavyat paścāt purastāta sakṛdavadāya bhṛguṇā madhyame kārṣmaryastatra carūṇāmuṣmāṇāṃ kriyate apalanayedyayorojaseti dvistūṣṇīṃ kuryātkarmagnyāvupahatiścetprā jāpatyaṃ vā prāyaścittaṃ juhuyāt | atītavicchinne tatkṣaṇe ṣaṣṭirdevatā hutvā ca tad ahorātramatītaṃ dramasauryaṣu ityeteṣu parvādyai svāmimavyame cetkartavyaṃ syāt prāyaścittir gṛhyāgnau karma kartumapi vāṇicaturthe rajaścāḍālānanugate vā saṃvatsarādūrdhvaṃ yathākṛcchraṃ vapanaṃ ca tathā prāyaścitti prāyaścittiḥ |
3.d: अथातः चरुपात्रं निरीक्ष्य संमुखे स्थापनं कार्यम् उदगुग्वास्य इत्येके संमुखे कार्यः चरोर्द्विभागं कार्यं स्रुवपात्रमासाद्य च्छिद्वानार्दं तदभावे कांस्यपात्रं वा तन्मध्ये ऽभिघार्य चरोः पूर्वदेशे सकृदवदाय द्वितीय्ये मध्यमे ह्यवदानं शेषे स्रुवपात्रे पुनश्चाभिधार्य अग्निमध्ये जुहुयात् त्वद्वितीयं चेञ्चरोः पश्चिमदेशे स्यात्सकृवदाय द्विभिघार्या प्रागुदग्देशे जुगुययाज् जामदग्न्याश्चेन्मव्यत् पश्चात् पुरस्तात सकृदवदाय भृगुणा मध्यमे कार्ष्मर्यस्तत्र चरूणामुष्माणां क्रियते अपलनयेद्ययोरोजसेति द्विस्तूष्णीं कुर्यात्कर्मग्न्यावुपहतिश्चेत्प्रा जापत्यं वा प्रायश्चित्तं जुहुयात् । अतीतविच्छिन्ने तत्क्षणे षष्टिर्देवता हुत्वा च तद् अहोरात्रमतीतं द्रमसौर्यषु इत्येतेषु पर्वाद्यै स्वामिमव्यमे चेत्कर्तव्यं स्यात् प्रायश्चित्तिर् गृह्याग्नौ कर्म कर्तुमपि वाणिचतुर्थे रजश्चाडालाननुगते वा संवत्सरादूर्ध्वं यथाकृच्छ्रं वपनं च तथा प्रायश्चित्ति प्रायश्चित्तिः ।
3.m:
Now then, having inspected the vessel of cooked oblation, it should be placed in front; some say it is to be moved to the north; it should be done in front; a division into two parts of the cooked oblation is to be made; having set down the sacrificial ladle [and] vessel […], in its absence, a bronze vessel; having basted the middle thereof, having cut off a portion once from the eastern part of the cooked oblation, a second portion cut off indeed in the middle part, having basted again with the remainder in the sacrificial ladle, he should offer it into the middle of the fire; and if the second [portion] is from the western part of the cooked oblation, having cut off a portion once, having basted twice, he should offer it in the north-eastern part; if they are descendants of Jamadagni, from the middle, the west, and the east, having cut off a portion once, [an oblation] is made of the heat of the cooked oblations by a descendant of Bhṛgu in the middle of kāmarṣya wood; he should remove [it]; with ‘By the strength of both’, he should do it twice silently; if there is an affliction in the two ritual fires, he should offer a Prājāpatya penance or an expiation.
When [an oblation] has lapsed and been omitted at that moment, having sacrificed to sixty deities, and that day and night has elapsed […], among these, if it is to be done on the new and full moon days by the master in the middle, it is an expiation; also to perform a rite in the domestic fire; or if in the fourth [month] [the wife] in her courses is not followed by an outcaste, after a year, as is the kṛcchra penance and tonsure, so is the expiation, the expiation.

4.d: अथ पर्वप्रायश्चित्तिरे उदगयनं वा दक्षिणायनं वा वसन्ताद्यादिषष्ठे चतुर्णां चान्द्रमाससौर्य इत्येतेषु पर्वाद्यैग्नामिष्टमध्ये चेत्कर्तव्यं स्यात्प्रायश्चित्तिर् गृह्याग्नौ कर्मार्तुमपि पाणिचतुर्थेहनि त्वदारभ्य तन्मा गादन्त उदयन दक्षिणाग्नौ चेष्टात्कर्तव्य तन्मासादिसंकल्पैः कर्तव्यं स्यात्प्रायश्चित्तिर् विवाहे यदि पूर्वपक्षे चेदपरे पौर्णमास्यैदारभ्य कर्तव्यः स्यात् संकल्पैर्दशपूर्णमासाभ्यां द्वाविष्टर इत्युक्तौ तत्र द्वितीया विष्टेदिना व्यादा यज्ञे ऽनर्थः तस्मात्ताभ्यां द्वाविष्टौरोपं विघ्नं कर्तव्यं स्यात्प्रायश्चित्ति नि तिसृभिश्चावमारयानि तां स्वधा मे विष्टिमध्या चेत्कर्तव्यं स्यात्प्रायश्चित्तिर् अनयोराघानमध्ये राहुपर्वणि चैन्द्रपमाह इति । आद्यपङ्कौ द्वितीया गायत्र्यां उभययोर्देवता चन्द्र इत्युक्त्वा प्रायश्चित्तिः । सौर्यः पर्वणि चेच्चित्रं देवानामुदु त्यामित्य आद्यैः त्रिष्टुप् त द्वितीये गायत्री वा उभयोर्देवता सूर्य इत्युक्त्वा प्रायश्चित्तिः प्रायश्चित्तं विना पुनश्चारम्भिणिं चेत् कर्तव्यं स्यात्प्रायश्चित्तिस् तां संकल्प्य मध्ये श्राद्धकर्माणि तत्राग्नौ करणं कपाणौ हुतं वा तद्वद् भुञ्जानः कर्तव्यं स्यात्प्रायश्चिर् अथ विशेषश्च नियमैर्दम्पत्योर्मध्ये रजश्चाण्डालगमने वा कर्तव्यं स्यात्प्रायश्चित्तिस् तयोराधानमध्ये राशौ मध्ये स्पर्शक्षयं वा वृद्धि वा कर्तव्यं स्यात्प्रायश्चित्तिस् तयोराधाममध्ये ऽन्यग्रामं प्रविश्य पथो गत्वा क्रतव्यं स्यात्प्रायश्चित्तिस्तयोर्मध्ये उभावन्यगमने वा दिवा मैथुने वा कर्तव्यं स्यात्प्रायश्चित्तिः पुरुषो भोजनमध्ये तथा कर्म मैथुनं च श्वानमार्जाला संस्पृष्ट्वा कर्तव्यं स्यात्प्रायश्चित्तिर् अथ विशेषश्च गृह्यावनग्निकानां च विधवां स्पृष्ट्वा कर्तव्यं स्यात्प्रायश्चित्तिर् अश्रोयी शूद्रान्तभोगो चार्वाको परदाराभिगमनो स्वकर्मत्यागो नित्यं परान्नभोजो तथानग्राहो गोब्रह्मणवधि वेश्यात्कुटुम्बी राजान्नभोजो अध्यापनग्रंथत्यागो विद्यादूष्यगुरुवादै प्राणसंहारी मार्जालोच्छिष्टभोजी वेदविक्रयो कन्यापतिव्रतादूषी स्वकुटुम्बत्यागी उपाध्यायगुरोर्दूषो गुरोः पत्न्याभिगमनी मांसभक्षी श्राद्धकालत्यागी तथा श्राद्धभोजी तठाकसंहारी वर्षवर्धी सदारागो ब्राह्मणताडो मृत्तिकापाषाणताही सदोच्छष्टो विप्रदूषो इति ते चंडालसमाः गृह्याग्नौ स्पृष्टा दंपत्योर्वासचेलं कार्यं कर्तव्यं स्यात्प्रायश्चित्ति प्रायश्चित्तार्थे षष्ठिदेवता उक्ता । कन्यहृतीनि व्याहृतिभिस्तृसृभिः आवृत्तिः पुनश्च तिसृभिर्द्वादशगुणं कार्यं प्राजापत्यं न पञ्चकसमस्तान्तं रि पाहि नो अग्रयेनसे इति तिसृभिः प्राजापत्यमेकं यत्कुसीदं च समस्तान्तं चतुर्थी स्विष्टकृद्वा इत्येषां प्रायश्चित्तिर्कं एवं ब्राह्मणेयो यासाः प्रायश्चित्तां विकतं जानन्यः शरीराद्विमुच्यते यः शरीराद्विमुच्यते ।
4.m: Now, the expiation for the joint days: whether in the northern course of the sun or the southern course of the sun, in the sixth [month] beginning with spring, among these four, lunar and solar—if [an omission] should occur in the middle of a sacrifice to the joint-day fires, an expiation must be performed. In the domestic fire, even for a rite in season, beginning on the fourth day of the hand[-taking], until that month has passed; if it should be performed in the southern course in the southern fire, an expiation must be performed with the intentions [set for] the beginning of that month. In a marriage, if in the first half of the month, or if in the other, it must be performed beginning from the full-moon day. With the intentions of the new- and full-moon sacrifices, when two sacrificial grass seats are prescribed, there, on the day of the second grass seat, opening the mouth, an obstruction [arises] in the sacrifice; therefore, an obstruction should be caused with those two grass seats. An expiation must be performed with three [mantras]; [one should offer] the avamārayās: if [an omission occurs] in the middle of those svadhā and viṣṭi [offerings], an expiation must be performed. During the establishment of these two [fires], or at an eclipse on a joint day: '[Agni,] tell Indra...' / With the first [verse] in the paṅkti [metre], and the second in the gāyatrī [metre], having stated: 'The deity for both is the Moon', the expiation [is performed]. / And if at a solar joint day [eclipse]: 'The wonderful face of the gods...' [and] 'Upward that [all-knowing god]...', with these initial [verses]—the first in the triṣṭubh [metre] and the second in the gāyatrī [metre]—having stated: 'The deity for both is the Sun', the expiation [is performed]. If one begins anew without an expiation, an expiation must be performed. Having intended that, in the middle of ancestral rites, if the offering is made there into the fire, or offered into the hand, eating in that manner, an expiation must be performed. Now, the special rule: by restrictive observances, if between the husband and wife there is menstruation or approach of a cāṇḍāla, an expiation must be performed. During the establishment of those two [fires], if in a heap [of grain] there is a decrease or an increase through touching, an expiation must be performed. During the establishment of those two [fires], having entered another village and traversed a path, an expiation must be performed. Between those two, if both go to another [partner] or in case of daytime sexual intercourse, an expiation must be performed. If a man, during eating, [engages in] such an act and sexual intercourse, or having touched a dog or a cat, an expiation must be performed. Now, a special rule: in the case of those without fire in the domestic sphere, having touched a widow, an expiation must be performed. One who is shelterless, one who enjoys the lower part of a śūdra woman, a Cārvāka, one who approaches another's wife, one who abandons one's own duty, one who constantly eats another's food, likewise one who takes what is not offered, a slayer of a cow or a brahmin, one whose family keeps prostitutes, one who eats a king's food, one who abandons the text of study, one who defames learning and disputes with the teacher, a destroyer of living beings, one who eats the remnants of a cat's food, a seller of the Veda, a defiler of a maiden and a chaste wife, one who abandons his own family, an abuser of an upādhyāya teacher, one who approaches the wife of a guru, an eater of meat, one who neglects the proper time for ancestral rites, likewise one who eats at an ancestral rite, a destroyer of a pond, one who lengthens [the measure of] rain, one who is always impassioned, a striker of a brahmin, a thrower of earth and stones, one who is always impure with food remnants, a slanderer of vipras—these are equal to cāṇḍālas. If touched at the domestic fire, the garment of the husband and wife must be [washed]; an expiation must be performed. For the purpose of expiation, sixty deities are declared. / With the three mystic utterances, repetition [is made]; again, with the three, it is to be made twelvefold. The Prājāpatya penance [consisting of five oblations] is not the fivefold one ending with the all-inclusive formula: with the three [verses], 'Protect us, Agni, from sin...', one Prājāpatya penance; and [the verse] 'Whatever debt [to Yama]...', ending with the all-inclusive formula; the fourth is the Sviṣṭakṛt offering. Such is the rite of expiation for these. Thus, knowing the specified expiation in the Brāhmaṇa, he is freed from the body, he who is freed from the body.

5.s: athātaḥ prāyaścittaviparyāsaḥsarvatra jalābhyāsaḥ prājāpatyaṃ yatkusīdaṃ ca saṃpūtyardhyāśabaliṃ hutvā yadi purastātta viparyāso yatkusīdaṃ juhuyāt yatsarvatra na saṃskārājyamapi yajamānaṃ hutvā tatanoṣaṃ bhavati adakṣiṇabrāhmaṇaṃ tadyajñorākṣasaṃ bhavati idmaṃ vinā yajate patati narake ubhau yajamāno brahmaṇā sarvatrāhutyā kālamanupekṣayā vipro yajñaghātakaḥ tisṛbhirbrahmaghātakaḥ tisṛbhiḥ saṃdhyākālānapekṣayā vipro jyotirghātakaḥ sarvatra pradoṣeṣvadhyāyo vedaghātaka anyāvarṇo vidyādānī gurughātakaḥ sarvatra svecchayātyāgīpitṛghātakaḥ ityete ityeteṣakhāpātikanā mātra bhāṣaṇaṃ nābhivādyamatra pathena śārśanaprekṣa iti yadi pramādākṛtvā gāyatryaṣṭa japet |
5.d: अथातः प्रायश्चित्तविपर्यासःसर्वत्र जलाभ्यासः प्राजापत्यं यत्कुसीदं च संपूत्यर्ध्याशबलिं हुत्वा यदि पुरस्तात्त विपर्यासो यत्कुसीदं जुहुयात् यत्सर्वत्र न संस्काराज्यमपि यजमानं हुत्वा ततनोषं भवति अदक्षिणब्राह्मणं तद्यज्ञोराक्षसं भवति इद्मं विना यजते पतति नरके उभौ यजमानो ब्रह्मणा सर्वत्राहुत्या कालमनुपेक्षया विप्रो यज्ञघातकः तिसृभिर्ब्रह्मघातकः तिसृभिः संध्याकालानपेक्षया विप्रो ज्योतिर्घातकः सर्वत्र प्रदोषेष्वध्यायो वेदघातक अन्यावर्णो विद्यादानी गुरुघातकः सर्वत्र स्वेच्छयात्यागीपितृघातकः इत्येते इत्येतेषखापातिकना मात्र भाषणं नाभिवाद्यमत्र पथेन शार्शनप्रेक्ष इति यदि प्रमादाकृत्वा गायत्र्यष्ट जपेत् ।
5.m: Now, the inversion of the expiations: everywhere, repeated use of water. Having completed the Prājāpatya penance and the 'Whatever debt [to Yama]...' [mantra] and offered the ardhyāśabali oblation: if prior to that there is an inversion, he should offer the 'Whatever debt [to Yama]...' [mantra]. When everywhere the clarified butter is not consecrated, having offered even the patron of the sacrifice, there is satisfaction. That sacrifice in which the brahmin receives no sacrificial fee becomes demonic. He who sacrifices without sacrificial firewood falls into hell—both the patron of the sacrifice and the priest. Everywhere, through disregarding the proper time for the oblation, a vipra is a destroyer of the sacrifice; with three [omissions], he is a slayer of a brahmin. Disregarding the time of twilight devotion, a vipra is a destroyer of the celestial light. Everywhere, study during the evening twilight is a destroyer of the Veda. Giving instruction to another caste is the destruction of a guru. Everywhere, one who abandons [his duties] by his own will is a slayer of his ancestors. These are those guilty of major sins; there should be no talking with them, nor should they be greeted with respectful salutation; on the road [one should not] look at their face. If done inadvertently, one should murmur the gāyatrī [verse] eight times.

6.s: dvibhāryāgnisaṃyogaḥ | athātaḥ sarvavarṇeṣu brāhmaṇānā punarādhipatyaṃ cet pūrvaṃ gṛhyāgnerardhaṃ praṇīya tayoḥ saṃyojanārthe caturthastyāhvaḥ sāyamupakramya yajamānaḥ pūrvāgnimavarohaṇaṃ kṛtvā tatra sthaṃḍilaṃ kurvana agniṃ vo vṛdhantamiti tṛcena pratiṣṭhāpyānantarabhāryā navāgnau pātreṇādāyemaṃ stomamiti tṛcena saṃyojya pratṛcāmante caturakṣarasupāṃśu tato agniraitviti ṣaḍbhirājyam hute yajamānaṃ vācayetprāṇāyāmaṃ pariṣicyāgnaye svāhā prajāpataye svāhā punaḥ pariṣicyāgauṣūkaṃ samāropaṇaṃ vāmadevyaṃ gītvā yadi deśāntare tatra laukikāgnau kuryātpūrvavat saṃyojyāpriyādhipatyaṃ cedviśeṣo 'sti tatra tadvyākhyāsyāmo brāhmaṇānāmantraya śatāpūpamāśayatakaṃ vāṣṭau snātvālaṃkṛtya kamaṇḍalunodakaṃ gṛhītvā vanāntare gatvā tasmindeśe aśuṣkāṃ komalīṃ śubhaparṇīṃ phalavatīṃ vistārayuktaṃ prāpahnīṃ sahittāṃ etairguṇavānarkaśākhāmavalokya tatpitrārthe vedavidbrāhmaṇaṃ vicārya snāpayitvārkaśākhā na haret navāsasācchādayitvā taṃ brāhmaṇo devasya tvetyarkakanyādānaṃ varaṃ pratigṛhṇāmīti purata sthaṇḍilaṃ kurvannarkasya uttarata upaviśya tāpaṣṭo brāhmaṇārkhaśākhāṃ pariveṣṭya sarve prāṅmukodaṅmukho vā brāhmaṇas tato brāhmaṇamabhyarcya pratyeka daśadaśāpūpaṃ dadyāt śeṣamuttaratī nidhāya laukikāgniṃ pratiṣṭhāpya tataḥ samūhanādi prapadāntaṃ kṛtvedhmāṅkaṃ hutvā tato vyāhṛtibhistisṛbhiḥ hutvā agniretviti ṣaḍbhiḥ punastisṛbhiḥ tato yajamānaḥ tiṣṭhannagni pradakṣiṇa gṛhya agnirāditya sarve brāhmaṇānāmantarbhāvaḥ ditvākāśayorbahirbhāvaḥ tūṣṇīṃ triḥ pradakṣiṇaṃ kuryāt svasthānamupaviśya dakṣiṇena sahitāraṃ gṛhṇīyāt tad gṛhṇāmi ta ityupāṃśu totopariṣṭāhomaṃ samāpya śiṣṭānapūpaṃ daśakaṃ brahmaṇe dadyāt daśakaṃ svayaṃ prāśrīyāt tatrāgnau pariṣicya abhyarcya vyāhṛtibhiśca tisṛbhiḥ ājyaṃ juhuyāt tadvisṛjya tato vāmadevyaṃ viprāṇāmāśiṣo vacaḥ kanyā gṛhaṃ gacchet tataḥ punarādhipatyaṃ punarādhipatyam |
6.d: द्विभार्याग्निसंयोगः । अथातः सर्ववर्णेषु ब्राह्मणाना पुनराधिपत्यं चेत् पूर्वं गृह्याग्नेरर्धं प्रणीय तयोः संयोजनार्थे चतुर्थस्त्याह्वः सायमुपक्रम्य यजमानः पूर्वाग्निमवरोहणं कृत्वा तत्र स्थंडिलं कुर्वन अग्निं वो वृधन्तमिति तृचेन प्रतिष्ठाप्यानन्तरभार्या नवाग्नौ पात्रेणादायेमं स्तोममिति तृचेन संयोज्य प्रतृचामन्ते चतुरक्षरसुपांशु ततो अग्निरैत्विति षड्भिराज्यम् हुते यजमानं वाचयेत्प्राणायामं परिषिच्याग्नये स्वाहा प्रजापतये स्वाहा पुनः परिषिच्यागौषूकं समारोपणं वामदेव्यं गीत्वा यदि देशान्तरे तत्र लौकिकाग्नौ कुर्यात्पूर्ववत् संयोज्याप्रियाधिपत्यं चेद्विशेषो ऽस्ति तत्र तद्व्याख्यास्यामो ब्राह्मणानामन्त्रय शतापूपमाशयतकं वाष्टौ स्नात्वालंकृत्य कमण्डलुनोदकं गृहीत्वा वनान्तरे गत्वा तस्मिन्देशे अशुष्कां कोमलीं शुभपर्णीं फलवतीं विस्तारयुक्तं प्रापह्नीं सहित्तां एतैर्गुणवानर्कशाखामवलोक्य तत्पित्रार्थे वेदविद्ब्राह्मणं विचार्य स्नापयित्वार्कशाखा न हरेत् नवाससाच्छादयित्वा तं ब्राह्मणो देवस्य त्वेत्यर्ककन्यादानं वरं प्रतिगृह्णामीति पुरत स्थण्डिलं कुर्वन्नर्कस्य उत्तरत उपविश्य तापष्टो ब्राह्मणार्खशाखां परिवेष्ट्य सर्वे प्राङ्मुकोदङ्मुखो वा ब्राह्मणस् ततो ब्राह्मणमभ्यर्च्य प्रत्येक दशदशापूपं दद्यात् शेषमुत्तरती निधाय लौकिकाग्निं प्रतिष्ठाप्य ततः समूहनादि प्रपदान्तं कृत्वेध्माङ्कं हुत्वा ततो व्याहृतिभिस्तिसृभिः हुत्वा अग्निरेत्विति षड्भिः पुनस्तिसृभिः ततो यजमानः तिष्ठन्नग्नि प्रदक्षिण गृह्य अग्निरादित्य सर्वे ब्राह्मणानामन्तर्भावः दित्वाकाशयोर्बहिर्भावः तूष्णीं त्रिः प्रदक्षिणं कुर्यात् स्वस्थानमुपविश्य दक्षिणेन सहितारं गृह्णीयात् तद् गृह्णामि त इत्युपांशु तोतोपरिष्टाहोमं समाप्य शिष्टानपूपं दशकं ब्रह्मणे दद्यात् दशकं स्वयं प्राश्रीयात् तत्राग्नौ परिषिच्य अभ्यर्च्य व्याहृतिभिश्च तिसृभिः आज्यं जुहुयात् तद्विसृज्य ततो वामदेव्यं विप्राणामाशिषो वचः कन्या गृहं गच्छेत् ततः पुनराधिपत्यं पुनराधिपत्यम् ।
6.m: The joining of the fires of two wives. / Now then, among all varnas, if there is remarriage for brahmins: having previously brought forward half of the domestic fire, for the purpose of joining them together, on the fourth day, having begun in the evening, the patron of the sacrifice, having caused the previous fire to descend, making a sacrificial ground there, having established [it] with the triplet beginning 'agniṃ vo vṛdhantam', taking the next wife's [fire] in a vessel to the new fire, having joined [them] with the triplet beginning 'imaṃ stomam', at the end of each triplet [reciting] four syllables in a whisper; then, clarified butter having been offered with the six [verses] beginning 'agnir aitu', he should make the patron of the sacrifice recite [the formula]; having controlled the breath, having sprinkled around, [he offers:] 'To Agni svāhā! To Prajāpati svāhā!'; having sprinkled around again, having performed the internalisation of the sacred fire, having sung the Vāmadevya; if in another region, he should perform it there in a common fire; having joined it as before, if there is marriage with a non-preferred [or supplementary bride], there is a special rule there; we shall explain that: having invited brahmins, he should feed them a hundred cakes, or eight; having bathed and adorned himself, taking water with a water pot, going into another forest, looking for an arka branch endowed with these qualities in that place: un-withered, tender, having auspicious leaves, bearing fruit, broad, facing eastward, possessing [vitality]; for the sake of its father, having examined a brahmin who knows the Veda, having bathed [the branch], he should not carry away the arka branch; having covered it with a new garment, the brahmin gives the gift of the arka maiden [saying] 'devasya tvā...'; [the groom says] 'I receive the bridegroom's [gift]'; making a sacrificial ground in front, sitting to the north of the arka [branch], having surrounded the arka branch with eight brahmins, all facing east or facing north, the brahmin, having then worshipped the brahmin, should give ten cakes to each; placing the remainder to the north, having established a common fire, having then performed [the rites] from the sweeping up to the introductory formula, having offered the limb of the sacrificial firewood, having then offered with the three mystic utterances, with the six [verses] beginning 'agnir aitu', [and] again with the three [mystic utterances]; then the patron of the sacrifice, standing, taking circumambulation from left to right of the fire, Agni and Āditya, [with] internalisation of all brahmins, [and] externalisation of heaven and earth, should silently perform circumambulation three times; sitting down in his own place, he should take the companion with his right hand; he recites in a whisper 'tad gṛhṇāmi te...'; then, having completed the later offerings, he should give ten remaining cakes to the priest, [and] himself should eat ten; having sprinkled around the fire there, having worshipped it, he should offer clarified butter with the three mystic utterances; having discharged that, then the Vāmadevya, the words of blessing of the brahmins; he should go to the maiden's house; then remarriage, remarriage.

7.s: atha ṛtukālaparokṣaṇam prathamārtavādanaḥ śuddhaḥ snātvā svastivācanaṃ śayyāgṛhamalaṃkṛtya puṣphalānvikīrya pratidiśaṃ dīpairalaṃkṛtya sugandhapaṅkena dīrghacaturasraṃ sthaṇḍilaṃ kurvan uparyukṣapatramudagagramāstīryāthopari navavāsasa prāgagrāmamāstīrya prāksiraḥ patnīṃ śayitvordhvamukhonathā jānubhyāṃ pādai vasumatyākramya tatsamīpe patis tatrābhimukho bhūtvovaśyesajastaitayo nimālabhya viṣṇuryoniṃ kalpayatviti aṣṭavāraṃ japitvāṣṭaputre bhavati skakāle patiralabhyaḥ cedanyapuruṣo na kartavyaṃ syāt ṣaḍrātro ṛtukālaḥ |
7.d: अथ ऋतुकालपरोक्षणम् प्रथमार्तवादनः शुद्धः स्नात्वा स्वस्तिवाचनं शय्यागृहमलंकृत्य पुष्फलान्विकीर्य प्रतिदिशं दीपैरलंकृत्य सुगन्धपङ्केन दीर्घचतुरस्रं स्थण्डिलं कुर्वन् उपर्युक्षपत्रमुदगग्रमास्तीर्याथोपरि नववासस प्रागग्राममास्तीर्य प्राक्सिरः पत्नीं शयित्वोर्ध्वमुखोनथा जानुभ्यां पादै वसुमत्याक्रम्य तत्समीपे पतिस् तत्राभिमुखो भूत्वोवश्येसजस्तैतयो निमालभ्य विष्णुर्योनिं कल्पयत्विति अष्टवारं जपित्वाष्टपुत्रे भवति स्ककाले पतिरलभ्यः चेदन्यपुरुषो न कर्तव्यं स्यात् षड्रात्रो ऋतुकालः ।
7.m: Now, the examination of the fertile period (ṛtukāla). Being purified after the first menses, having bathed, [performing] the recitation of auspicious blessings, having adorned the bed-chamber, having scattered flowers and fruits, having decorated each direction with lamps, making an oblong sacrificial ground with fragrant paste, having strewn upon it palāśa leaves with their tips pointing northward, and having strewn a new cloth above it with its ends pointing eastward, having made his wife lie down with her head to the east and face turned upward, stepping upon the earth with knees and feet, near her, the husband, facing towards her there, touching her organ, having muttered eight times 'May Viṣṇu prepare the womb' (viṣṇur yoniṃ kalpayatu), there will be eight sons; at the proper time the husband is to be approached; another man must not be taken; the fertile period lasts six nights.

8.s: athāto garbhasaṃskāro maithunaṣaṣṭhe pratidinaprabhṛti yugme dine yagmāsu putro jāyoran yugmāsu putro jāyeran ayugmāsu rātriṣu striyo jāyeran iti jñātvā yadā vadhvāḥ prathamagarbho bhavati tadodarasaṃskārādvāreṇotpatsyamānāpatyasaṃskārārthaṃ puṃsavanasīmantonnayanaṃ kuryād yā kutrāciddine garbhasaṃbhavastanmāsamekaṃ gaṇayitvā tṛtīyamāsāṃstvavaśobhanaṃ tataḥ puṃsavanaṃ nāndīmukhaṃ pūrve 'hani tataḥ pare 'hanyuṣasi snātvā caturasraṃ sthaṇḍilamupalipyodagagreśi darbheṣūpaviśya dakṣiṇataḥ patnīṃ cottarato yajamānodaṅmukho brāhmaṇas tato 'gneḥ praṇayanaṃ vā vinā prātarāhutiṃ hutvā samūhanādippadānta hutvā idhmāṅgaṃ hutvā tato vyāhṛtibhiḥ tisṛbhirhutvā tato yajamānaḥ patnyā pṛṣṭhatastiṣṭhat dakṣiṇakoryarādi nābhyankamamimṛśet pumāṃsāviti brūyāt svasthānamupaviśya tatopariṣṭāddhomaṃ samāpya vadhvāṃ punaḥ snātvā yajamānaḥ puṣpākṣatānekaviṃśatiyavānnavaśūpe nidhāya gṛhītvā grāmānniṣkramay vaṭarājasamīpaṃ gatvā tatra vāsinīmupasthāyotsāhavyāpinītyadrame nityagasthiterāpitsataṃ me śriyaṃ dehi tasmānnamābhīṣṭaṃ kurvantviti puṣpākṣatairabhyarcya tasyopari yavairavakīryodagagrāṃ śākhāṃ paraśunā cchedayitvā tamoṣadhobhūmau navāntarikṣe vā gṛhṇīyād ūrdhvāgrāṃ gṛhamānīya koṣṭhamadhye maṇikadeśe vā svāsane pratiṣṭāpyaṃ tataścaturasraṃ sthaṇḍilamupalipya brūyavetkimārgaṇā prapadāntaṃ kṛtvā idhmāṅgaṃ hutvā punaśca vyāhṛtibhistasṛbhirhutvā tamoṣadhessaptabhirmukhalakanyā bhrātumato prāṅmukho peṣayitvā pratyāharantīṃ taṃ pratiṣṭaṃ navavo saśrinanakṣi japet gṛhītvā yajamānaḥ tatoṣa'gneḥ paścātpatnīṃ prākśirordhvamukhīṃ śayitvāvadhvāgnyormadhye yajamānaḥ pratyaṅmukhaḥ sāyīta punānagniriti mantreṇa dakṣiṇanāsikāpuṭe piṣṭarasaṃ pīḍayitvā niṣpoḍya piṣṭaṃ salile nidhāya vastraṃ brahmaṇe dadyāt tadrasamudare kuryāt tayoḥ svasthānamupaviśya tatopariṣṭādi samāpyala tato brāhmaṇabhojanaṃ tato brāhmaṇabhojanam |
8.d: अथातो गर्भसंस्कारो मैथुनषष्ठे प्रतिदिनप्रभृति युग्मे दिने यग्मासु पुत्रो जायोरन् युग्मासु पुत्रो जायेरन् अयुग्मासु रात्रिषु स्त्रियो जायेरन् इति ज्ञात्वा यदा वध्वाः प्रथमगर्भो भवति तदोदरसंस्काराद्वारेणोत्पत्स्यमानापत्यसंस्कारार्थं पुंसवनसीमन्तोन्नयनं कुर्याद् या कुत्राचिद्दिने गर्भसंभवस्तन्मासमेकं गणयित्वा तृतीयमासांस्त्ववशोभनं ततः पुंसवनं नान्दीमुखं पूर्वे ऽहनि ततः परे ऽहन्युषसि स्नात्वा चतुरस्रं स्थण्डिलमुपलिप्योदगग्रेशि दर्भेषूपविश्य दक्षिणतः पत्नीं चोत्तरतो यजमानोदङ्मुखो ब्राह्मणस् ततो ऽग्नेः प्रणयनं वा विना प्रातराहुतिं हुत्वा समूहनादिप्पदान्त हुत्वा इध्माङ्गं हुत्वा ततो व्याहृतिभिः तिसृभिर्हुत्वा ततो यजमानः पत्न्या पृष्ठतस्तिष्ठत् दक्षिणकोर्यरादि नाभ्यन्कममिमृशेत् पुमांसाविति ब्रूयात् स्वस्थानमुपविश्य ततोपरिष्टाद्धोमं समाप्य वध्वां पुनः स्नात्वा यजमानः पुष्पाक्षतानेकविंशतियवान्नवशूपे निधाय गृहीत्वा ग्रामान्निष्क्रमय् वटराजसमीपं गत्वा तत्र वासिनीमुपस्थायोत्साहव्यापिनीत्यद्रमे नित्यगस्थितेरापित्सतं मे श्रियं देहि तस्मान्नमाभीष्टं कुर्वन्त्विति पुष्पाक्षतैरभ्यर्च्य तस्योपरि यवैरवकीर्योदगग्रां शाखां परशुना च्छेदयित्वा तमोषधोभूमौ नवान्तरिक्षे वा गृह्णीयाद् ऊर्ध्वाग्रां गृहमानीय कोष्ठमध्ये मणिकदेशे वा स्वासने प्रतिष्टाप्यं ततश्चतुरस्रं स्थण्डिलमुपलिप्य ब्रूयवेत्किमार्गणा प्रपदान्तं कृत्वा इध्माङ्गं हुत्वा पुनश्च व्याहृतिभिस्तसृभिर्हुत्वा तमोषधेस्सप्तभिर्मुखलकन्या भ्रातुमतो प्राङ्मुखो पेषयित्वा प्रत्याहरन्तीं तं प्रतिष्टं नववो सश्रिननक्षि जपेत् गृहीत्वा यजमानः ततोषऽग्नेः पश्चात्पत्नीं प्राक्शिरोर्ध्वमुखीं शयित्वावध्वाग्न्योर्मध्ये यजमानः प्रत्यङ्मुखः सायीत पुनानग्निरिति मन्त्रेण दक्षिणनासिकापुटे पिष्टरसं पीडयित्वा निष्पोड्य पिष्टं सलिले निधाय वस्त्रं ब्रह्मणे दद्यात् तद्रसमुदरे कुर्यात् तयोः स्वस्थानमुपविश्य ततोपरिष्टादि समाप्यल ततो ब्राह्मणभोजनं ततो ब्राह्मणभोजनम् ।
8.m: Now then, the consecration of the fetus: from the sixth day of sexual union onwards, knowing that sons are born on even days, sons are born on even [nights], [and] daughters are born on uneven nights, when it is the bride's first pregnancy, through the consecration of the womb, for the sake of consecrating the offspring about to be born, he should perform the puṃsavana and the sīmantonnayana; counting one month from whatever day conception occurred, in the third month, on an auspicious day, then the puṃsavana; the ancestral offering for prosperity on the preceding day; then, on the following day at dawn, having bathed, having smeared a four-cornered sacrificial ground, sitting upon darbha grass with tips to the north, the wife to the south and the patron of the sacrifice to the north, facing east, the brahmin priest, then having brought forward the fire or without it, having offered the morning oblation, having offered [the rites] from the sweeping up to the introductory formula, having offered the limb of the sacrificial firewood, having then offered with the three mystic utterances; then the patron of the sacrifice, standing behind his wife, should touch her right waist down to the navel, saying 'Two males!'; sitting down in his own place, then having completed the later offerings, the bride having bathed again, the patron of the sacrifice, having placed flowers, unbroken grains, and twenty-one barley grains in a new winnowing basket, taking it, going out from the village, having gone near the king of banyan trees, having approached the goddess residing there, [praying] 'O pervasive with vigour... grant me enduring prosperity, therefore may they fulfil my desire!', having worshipped with flowers and unbroken grains, having scattered barley over it, having cut a branch with its tip to the north using an axe, he should catch that herb either above the ground or in the mid-air; having brought it home with its tip upward, having installed it in the middle of the storehouse or in the place of the water-jar on a proper seat, then having smeared a square sacrificial ground, having performed [the rites] up to the introductory formula, having offered the limb of the sacrificial firewood, and again having offered with the three mystic utterances, having had that herb ground by an auspicious maiden or a brother facing east, taking it as she brings it, the patron of the sacrifice should mutter [the verse]...; then, having made the wife lie down to the west of the fire with her head to the east and face turned upward, the patron of the sacrifice should lie between the bride and the fire facing west; pressing the juice of the paste into the right nostril with the mantra beginning 'punānagnir', having squeezed it out, placing the paste in water, he should give the garment to the brahmin; she should take that juice into her stomach; both sitting in their own places, then having completed the later offerings, then feeding of brahmins, then feeding of brahmins.

9.s: atha caturthe māsi sīmantonnayanaṃ kartavyam nāndīmukhaṃ pūrve 'hani tataḥ pare 'hanyuṣasi snātvā yajamānaḥ puṃsavanaṃ krameṇaudumbanaśākhāṃ gṛhamānīya triśvetayā ca śalalyā taṇḍulān tilamiśrān śrapayitvā laukike 'gnau sthaṇḍilasyottarato nidhāya pūrvavatprapadāntaṃ kṛtvā idhmāṅgaṃ hutvā punaśca vyāhṛtibhistisṛbhirhutvā tato yajāmānaḥ pṛṣṭhastiṣṭhan taṃ gṛhītvā audumbaraśākhāmayamūrjati vā japitvā nāsāgrameti didhyaṃnnisnāranātamunnayadantimatho yenīditeti pratipya punaḥ śalalyā gṛhītvā rākā ityeke iti pratiṣṭhāp. tūṣṇīṃ triḥ prokṣaṇaṃ kṛtvā svasthānamupaviśya tatopariṣṭāddhomānsamāpya vadha dhṛtapātrā kiṃ paśyasīti vācayitvā vāmadevya gotvā tato brāhmaṇabhojanaṃ tato brāhmaṇabhojanam |
9.d: अथ चतुर्थे मासि सीमन्तोन्नयनं कर्तव्यम् नान्दीमुखं पूर्वे ऽहनि ततः परे ऽहन्युषसि स्नात्वा यजमानः पुंसवनं क्रमेणौदुम्बनशाखां गृहमानीय त्रिश्वेतया च शलल्या तण्डुलान् तिलमिश्रान् श्रपयित्वा लौकिके ऽग्नौ स्थण्डिलस्योत्तरतो निधाय पूर्ववत्प्रपदान्तं कृत्वा इध्माङ्गं हुत्वा पुनश्च व्याहृतिभिस्तिसृभिर्हुत्वा ततो यजामानः पृष्ठस्तिष्ठन् तं गृहीत्वा औदुम्बरशाखामयमूर्जति वा जपित्वा नासाग्रमेति दिध्यंन्निस्नारनातमुन्नयदन्तिमथो येनीदितेति प्रतिप्य पुनः शलल्या गृहीत्वा राका इत्येके इति प्रतिष्ठाप्. तूष्णीं त्रिः प्रोक्षणं कृत्वा स्वस्थानमुपविश्य ततोपरिष्टाद्धोमान्समाप्य वध धृतपात्रा किं पश्यसीति वाचयित्वा वामदेव्य गोत्वा ततो ब्राह्मणभोजनं ततो ब्राह्मणभोजनम् ।
9.m: Now, in the fourth month, the parting of the hair (sīmantonnayana) should be performed. The ancestral offering for prosperity (nāndīmukha) [is performed] on the preceding day. Then, having bathed at dawn on the following day, the patron of the sacrifice, following the sequence of the rite for producing a male child (puṃsavana), brings an udumbara branch to the house. And having cooked rice grains mixed with sesame with a porcupine quill that has three white rings on the common fire, and having placed it to the north of the sacrificial ground, having performed [the ritual] up to the introductory formula (prapada) as before, having made the offering of the kindling sticks (idhmāṅga), and having offered again with the three mystic utterances (vyāhṛti); then the patron of the sacrifice, standing behind, taking that udumbara branch, or having muttered 'ayam ūrjā...', looking at the tip of the nose, parts [her hair upwards]... having said 'yenāditih...'; taking [it] again with the quill, according to some [with the verse to] Rākā; establishing [it], having silently performed consecration by sprinkling three times, sitting in his own place, then having completed the subsequent offerings, having made the wife who holds the vessel say, 'What do you see?', having sung the Vāmadevya chant, then the feeding of brahmins, then the feeding of brahmins.

10.s: atha putrasya jananakāle soṣyantīhomārabhe ekadeśapraṇayana snātvā sthaṇḍilamupalipya samūhanādi prapadāntaṃ kṛtvā idhmāṅgaṃ hutvā tataḥ śirojananakāle yātiraśvīti dvābhyāmājyaṃ hutvāsau śabde nāma brūyāt putro vārabhamavenmuniśraṣṭha pṛcchāmi tvā mitvātprivās tadenāmagrahaṇaṃ karaṇātpūrvaṃ kṛtakāni nāmāni tatkathaṃ vistareṇa tathyaṃ me brūhya aśeṣaṃ tu vyākhyāsyāmo nī karaṇā davamimamañcakaṃ nā paścānpūtrakaṃ kuryād yadi viparyāsonmāyenākṛtaṃ cetaṃ hutaṃmamarghatasmājjanavadunta yatrābhāvaḥ tyasyā prāyaścittaṃ juhuyād ava vā janana iṣvāṃte sauśabde viṣṇupradevaśarmanniti manasā kalpayan manasaṃ praviśayāsauśabde vivādabīyaṃ brūyān ko nāmāsya asau śabde nakṣatraśrayaṃ nāma kartavyam maghaṃ vā putrayorekatra yānanād yadi jātakarmādi nāpataṃ saṃskārameva kartavyaṃ nāmakaraṇādūrdhvaṃ pṛthak saṃskāraṃ svayaṃ kuryāt jātakarma vakṣyāmi daśayanāpra iti ṣayitvā trayastriṃśadbīhīti madhusarpibhyāmekaikaṃ palamādāya ubhayatra yaśaso yaśaso 'sīti saṃyojya hiraṇyaśakalena samamaṅguṣṭhābhyāṃ anāmikābhyāṃ vā saṃgṛhya tadabhāve kuśayevā yavapiṣṭamājyadvayamākṣeti śiśaṃ prataya taṃdvasarpibhyāṃ medhāṃ ta iti tato brāhmaṇadakṣiṇā |
10.d: अथ पुत्रस्य जननकाले सोष्यन्तीहोमारभे एकदेशप्रणयन स्नात्वा स्थण्डिलमुपलिप्य समूहनादि प्रपदान्तं कृत्वा इध्माङ्गं हुत्वा ततः शिरोजननकाले यातिरश्वीति द्वाभ्यामाज्यं हुत्वासौ शब्दे नाम ब्रूयात् पुत्रो वारभमवेन्मुनिश्रष्ठ पृच्छामि त्वा मित्वात्प्रिवास् तदेनामग्रहणं करणात्पूर्वं कृतकानि नामानि तत्कथं विस्तरेण तथ्यं मे ब्रूह्य अशेषं तु व्याख्यास्यामो नी करणा दवमिममञ्चकं ना पश्चान्पूत्रकं कुर्याद् यदि विपर्यासोन्मायेनाकृतं चेतं हुतंममर्घतस्माज्जनवदुन्त यत्राभावः त्यस्या प्रायश्चित्तं जुहुयाद् अव वा जनन इष्वांते सौशब्दे विष्णुप्रदेवशर्मन्निति मनसा कल्पयन् मनसं प्रविशयासौशब्दे विवादबीयं ब्रूयान् को नामास्य असौ शब्दे नक्षत्रश्रयं नाम कर्तव्यम् मघं वा पुत्रयोरेकत्र याननाद् यदि जातकर्मादि नापतं संस्कारमेव कर्तव्यं नामकरणादूर्ध्वं पृथक् संस्कारं स्वयं कुर्यात् जातकर्म वक्ष्यामि दशयनाप्र इति षयित्वा त्रयस्त्रिंशद्बीहीति मधुसर्पिभ्यामेकैकं पलमादाय उभयत्र यशसो यशसो ऽसीति संयोज्य हिरण्यशकलेन सममङ्गुष्ठाभ्यां अनामिकाभ्यां वा संगृह्य तदभावे कुशयेवा यवपिष्टमाज्यद्वयमाक्षेति शिशं प्रतय तंद्वसर्पिभ्यां मेधां त इति ततो ब्राह्मणदक्षिणा ।
10.m:
Now, at the time of the birth of a son, he begins the offering for the woman in labour (soṣyantīhoma). Having brought [fire] from one portion, having bathed, having smeared the sacrificial ground, having performed [the rites] from the sweeping up to the introductory formula (prapada), having made the offering of the kindling sticks (idhmāṅga); then at the time of the emergence of the head, having offered clarified butter with the two [verses], 'yātir aśvī...', at the word 'asau' ('so-and-so') he should speak the name... [...] at the word 'asau' a name connected with a lunar asterism should be given, or 'Magha'... after the naming ceremony, he should himself perform the rite separately.
I shall describe the birth-rite (jātakarma): [...] taking one pala each of honey and clarified butter, joining them both together with 'yaśaso yaśaso 'si...', grasping together with a piece of gold with the two thumbs or the two ring fingers—in the absence of that, with kuśa grass—or barley flour mixed with clarified butter... with honey and clarified butter with 'medhāṃ te...'; then the priestly fee to the brahmin.

11.s: tataścandradarśam | jananādi daśarātrātpare dve vā tasminnakṣatre taṃ kumāraṃ syātitātaṃ vetadūrdhakimāṃsuśadarśanaṃ tadabhāvaṃ darśanaṃ kṛtvā cāma kuryāt kathaṃ vakṣyāmi nāndomukhaṃ pūrva'hani tataḥ ahanyuṣasi snātvā yajamānaścaturasraṃ sthaṇḍilamupalipya gṛhyāgnerekadeśāgni vibhajya samūhanādi prapadāntaṃ kṛtvā idhmāṅgaṃ hutvā tato mātā svakumāramādāyāhatena vāsā parighāya dakṣiṇataḥ pratyaṅmukhaḥ upaviśya tatkārayitvā patihaste pradāya pṛṣṭhato gatvottarato upaviśya yajamānasvaṃ kumāraṃ avalokya vyāhṛtibhistisṛbhirhutvā punaḥ pradāya yajamāno paṃcāṃ madhyena ko 'sīti dvābhyāmarakṣaṇā pratinetramabhimṛśet katamo 'sīti caturakṣareṇa śrotrābhyāṃ eṣo 'sīti tryakṣareṇa nāsāgre madhyamūlamabhimṛśed amṛtosīti caturakṣareṇa pāṇibāhubhyāṃ pratyekamabhimṛśed amṛtosīti caturakṣareṇa pāṇibāhubhyāṃ pratyekamabhimṛśya śeṣeṇa mastakaṃ gṛhītvā tato mātā ca vāmahastena kumāryavakaṃ gṛhitvā pūrvoktamākhyānaṃ dakṣiṇaṃ śravaṇe upāṃśu brūyāt tato yajamāno dakṣiṇaṃ gṛhṇīyāt tata upāṃśu sarvānhetyativādanīyaṃ nāma brūyāt tata upariṣṭāddhomaṃ samāpya yathā vāmadevyaṃgītvā pativartāśiṣo vācayitvā tathā brāhmaṇabhojanam |
11.d: ततश्चन्द्रदर्शम् । जननादि दशरात्रात्परे द्वे वा तस्मिन्नक्षत्रे तं कुमारं स्यातितातं वेतदूर्धकिमांसुशदर्शनं तदभावं दर्शनं कृत्वा चाम कुर्यात् कथं वक्ष्यामि नान्दोमुखं पूर्वऽहनि ततः अहन्युषसि स्नात्वा यजमानश्चतुरस्रं स्थण्डिलमुपलिप्य गृह्याग्नेरेकदेशाग्नि विभज्य समूहनादि प्रपदान्तं कृत्वा इध्माङ्गं हुत्वा ततो माता स्वकुमारमादायाहतेन वासा परिघाय दक्षिणतः प्रत्यङ्मुखः उपविश्य तत्कारयित्वा पतिहस्ते प्रदाय पृष्ठतो गत्वोत्तरतो उपविश्य यजमानस्वं कुमारं अवलोक्य व्याहृतिभिस्तिसृभिर्हुत्वा पुनः प्रदाय यजमानो पंचां मध्येन को ऽसीति द्वाभ्यामरक्षणा प्रतिनेत्रमभिमृशेत् कतमो ऽसीति चतुरक्षरेण श्रोत्राभ्यां एषो ऽसीति त्र्यक्षरेण नासाग्रे मध्यमूलमभिमृशेद् अमृतोसीति चतुरक्षरेण पाणिबाहुभ्यां प्रत्येकमभिमृशेद् अमृतोसीति चतुरक्षरेण पाणिबाहुभ्यां प्रत्येकमभिमृश्य शेषेण मस्तकं गृहीत्वा ततो माता च वामहस्तेन कुमार्यवकं गृहित्वा पूर्वोक्तमाख्यानं दक्षिणं श्रवणे उपांशु ब्रूयात् ततो यजमानो दक्षिणं गृह्णीयात् तत उपांशु सर्वान्हेत्यतिवादनीयं नाम ब्रूयात् तत उपरिष्टाद्धोमं समाप्य यथा वामदेव्यंगीत्वा पतिवर्ताशिषो वाचयित्वा तथा ब्राह्मणभोजनम् ।
11.m:
Then the moon-viewing rite (candradarśana).
After ten nights from the birth, or on the second [day], or on that [same] lunar asterism, that boy... I shall describe how: the ancestral offering for prosperity (nāndīmukha) [is performed] on the preceding day; then, having bathed at dawn on the [following] day, the patron of the sacrifice, having smeared a four-cornered sacrificial ground, having divided the fire from a portion of the domestic fire, having performed [the rites] from the sweeping up to the introductory formula (prapada), having made the offering of the kindling sticks (idhmāṅga); then the mother, taking her boy, clothed in unwashed garments, sitting on the south facing west, having caused that to be done, placing [him] into the hand of her husband, having gone behind, sits on the north. The patron of the sacrifice, looking at his boy, having offered with the three mystic utterances (vyāhṛti), having handed [him] back, the patron of the sacrifice touches each eye with the middle of the five [fingers] with the two [formulas], 'ko 'si...'; touches the two ears with the four-syllable [formula], 'katamo 'si...'; touches the root of the middle of the tip of the nose with the three-syllable [formula], 'eṣo 'si...'; touches each hand and arm with the four-syllable [formula], 'amṛto 'si...'; having touched each hand and arm with the four-syllable [formula], 'amṛto 'si...', having taken the head with the remainder; then the mother, taking the boy with her left hand, should whisper the aforesaid appellation into his right ear. Then the patron of the sacrifice should take the right [ear/hand]. Then he should speak in a low voice the name used in greeting. Then, having completed the subsequent offerings, having sung the Vāmadevya chant according to rule, having caused the chaste wife to recite blessings, then the feeding of brahmins.

12.s: athātaścandropasthānam śuklapakṣatṛtīyāpañcamyāṃ spatamyāṃ ṣaṣṭhe vāṣṭame vā nuvakṣyādinā kartavyaṃ syāt tṛtīye māsi ṣaṣṭhe māsi kāryaṃ pañcāṅgaśodhite dine | chandogaṃ vedavidbrāhmaṇaṃ niyakṣā sadbrāhmaṇa udayādarvāk grāmānniṣkramya saśirataṃ sthāpayitvā śaketā svarṇakalaśamādāya kāṃśya vā mṛnmayavarja jānumātramavagāhyāpo hi ṣṭhati tṛcona pūrayitvā śannī devoriti mantreṇāddhṛtyamiti śirasi vinidhāya yaḥ pāvamānoriti jalaṃ niṣkramya vāmadevyena grāmaṃ praviśet sarvatra na saṃbhāṣaṇaṃ nopahyasya sumunaso bhūtvā yajamānagṛhe devasabhāsamīpe goṣṭamadhye vā tāmudapātrāṃ cāsane nidhāyopari kuśaiḥ chādayitvā taṃ brāhmaṇayajamānādivāvabhujjan yāntī vā ityete āstamayād ahassahasirasaṃ sthāpayitvā tatra yajamānaḥ niṣkramya gṛhādbahiḥ śucau deśe caturasraṃ sthaṇḍilamupalipya dakṣiṇābhimukho bhūtvā hā u ya candreti maṇḍalaṃ praviśya prāṅmukhopaviśya svastivācanaṃ kṛtvā yajamānaṃ puṣpāñjaliṃ pūrayitvā candrābhimukhastiṣṭhan tato mātā ca kumāramuddhṛtya dakṣiṇataḥ pratyaṅmukhobhūtvā taṃ kumāraṃ pratihaste pradāya pṛṣṭhato gatvottarataḥ tiṣṭhed yajamānaḥ puṣpāñjalyuparikumāraṃ dhārayatyate sukomaṃta iti tisṛbhirupasthāyodañca mātre pradāya karābhyāmañjaliṃ kuryāt tamañjaliṃ brahmapraṇavena pūrayitvā padaścedapāñjaliṃ avasicet punastūṣṇīṃ pūrayitvā tathā dvistūṣṇīmutsṛjya pratyaṅmukhopaviśya vāmadevyaṃ gītvā tato brāhmaṇabhojanaṃ tato brāhmaṇabhojanam |
12.d: अथातश्चन्द्रोपस्थानम् शुक्लपक्षतृतीयापञ्चम्यां स्पतम्यां षष्ठे वाष्टमे वा नुवक्ष्यादिना कर्तव्यं स्यात् तृतीये मासि षष्ठे मासि कार्यं पञ्चाङ्गशोधिते दिने । छन्दोगं वेदविद्ब्राह्मणं नियक्षा सद्ब्राह्मण उदयादर्वाक् ग्रामान्निष्क्रम्य सशिरतं स्थापयित्वा शकेता स्वर्णकलशमादाय कांश्य वा मृन्मयवर्ज जानुमात्रमवगाह्यापो हि ष्ठति तृचोन पूरयित्वा शन्नी देवोरिति मन्त्रेणाद्धृत्यमिति शिरसि विनिधाय यः पावमानोरिति जलं निष्क्रम्य वामदेव्येन ग्रामं प्रविशेत् सर्वत्र न संभाषणं नोपह्यस्य सुमुनसो भूत्वा यजमानगृहे देवसभासमीपे गोष्टमध्ये वा तामुदपात्रां चासने निधायोपरि कुशैः छादयित्वा तं ब्राह्मणयजमानादिवावभुज्जन् यान्ती वा इत्येते आस्तमयाद् अहस्सहसिरसं स्थापयित्वा तत्र यजमानः निष्क्रम्य गृहाद्बहिः शुचौ देशे चतुरस्रं स्थण्डिलमुपलिप्य दक्षिणाभिमुखो भूत्वा हा उ य चन्द्रेति मण्डलं प्रविश्य प्राङ्मुखोपविश्य स्वस्तिवाचनं कृत्वा यजमानं पुष्पाञ्जलिं पूरयित्वा चन्द्राभिमुखस्तिष्ठन् ततो माता च कुमारमुद्धृत्य दक्षिणतः प्रत्यङ्मुखोभूत्वा तं कुमारं प्रतिहस्ते प्रदाय पृष्ठतो गत्वोत्तरतः तिष्ठेद् यजमानः पुष्पाञ्जल्युपरिकुमारं धारयत्यते सुकोमंत इति तिसृभिरुपस्थायोदञ्च मात्रे प्रदाय कराभ्यामञ्जलिं कुर्यात् तमञ्जलिं ब्रह्मप्रणवेन पूरयित्वा पदश्चेदपाञ्जलिं अवसिचेत् पुनस्तूष्णीं पूरयित्वा तथा द्विस्तूष्णीमुत्सृज्य प्रत्यङ्मुखोपविश्य वामदेव्यं गीत्वा ततो ब्राह्मणभोजनं ततो ब्राह्मणभोजनम् ।
12.m:
Now, therefore, the reverence of the moon (candropasthāna). It should be performed on the third, fifth, seventh, or sixth or eighth lunar day of the bright fortnight, as will be explained; it is to be done in the third month or in the sixth month on a day purified according to the five astrological components (pañcāṅga).
Having appointed a Sāmavedic chanter (chandoga), a brahmin who knows the Veda, that good brahmin, going forth from the village before sunrise, having placed [the vessel] with its top... taking a golden water vessel, or a bronze one, avoiding an earthen one, having waded knee-deep into the water, having filled it with the triplet 'āpo hi ṣṭhā...', having lifted it up with the mantra 'śaṃ no devīḥ...', having placed it on his head, having stepped out of the water with 'yaḥ pāvamānīḥ...', he should enter the village with the Vāmadevya chant. Nowhere should there be conversation, nor should he smile; being cheerful, having placed that water vessel on a seat in the house of the patron of the sacrifice, near an assembly of the gods, or in the middle of a cow-pen, and having covered it on top with kuśa grass... until sunset... standing there, the patron of the sacrifice, having gone outside the house, having smeared a four-cornered sacrificial ground in a clean place, facing south, having entered the circle with 'hā u ya candra...', sitting facing east, having performed the recitation of auspicious blessings (svastivācana), having filled the hands of the patron of the sacrifice with a handful of flowers (puṣpāñjali), standing facing the moon; then the mother also, having lifted up the boy, being on the south facing west, having handed that boy into the hand of her husband, having gone behind, should stand on the north. The patron of the sacrifice holds the boy above the handful of flowers; having revered [the moon] with the three [verses], '...'; having handed [the child] facing north to the mother, he should make a hollow of his hands. Having filled that hollow of the hands with the sacred syllable (praṇava), he should pour out the hollow of water line by line. Having filled it again silently, having likewise poured it out silently twice, sitting facing west, having sung the Vāmadevya chant, then the feeding of brahmins, then the feeding of brahmins.

13.s: ṣaṣṭhe māsyannaprāśanam abhyūdayikam pūrve 'hani pare 'hanyuṣasi snātvā yajamāno yavapiṣṭaṃ vā pāyasaṃ śrapayitvā kriyāmakriyāmataṇḍulāṃ svarūpatvaṃ pitā tatye mātā ca kumāramādāyopaviśya jātakamavat karmārambhe pāyasaṃ prāśnoyāt tato brāhṇabhojanaṃ tato brāhmaṇabhojanam |
13.d: षष्ठे मास्यन्नप्राशनम् अभ्यूदयिकम् पूर्वे ऽहनि परे ऽहन्युषसि स्नात्वा यजमानो यवपिष्टं वा पायसं श्रपयित्वा क्रियामक्रियामतण्डुलां स्वरूपत्वं पिता तत्ये माता च कुमारमादायोपविश्य जातकमवत् कर्मारम्भे पायसं प्राश्नोयात् ततो ब्राह्णभोजनं ततो ब्राह्मणभोजनम् ।
13.m: In the sixth month is the first feeding of solid food. The ancestral offering for prosperity is on the preceding day. On the following day, having bathed at dawn, the patron of the sacrifice cooks barley meal or rice boiled in milk. Whether [regular] rites [have been performed] or not, [with grain] husked into its natural state, the father and the mother, taking the boy and sitting down as at the birth-rite, shall feed him the rice boiled in milk at the beginning of the ceremony. Then the feeding of brahmins; then the feeding of brahmins.

14.s: tṛtīye varṣe vapanaṃ kāryam ābhyudāyikaṃ pūrve 'hni tataḥ pare 'hanyuṣasi snātvā yajamānaḥ caturasraṃ sthaṇḍilamupaliṣya maṇḍalādbahirdakṣiṇenā'jyāgneyādi sthāpayitvā nāpitaḥ prāṅmukhopaviśya tatoṣṇopayātrāmādarśe tadanvantaraṃ bhātkacaṃ tat paśmimena darbhaṃ piñjūlī śthaṇḍilasyottare vāyavyādi snāpayitvā raktānaḍugomayaṃ laukikatvaṃ kṛsarasthālīpāko vṛthāpakva iti homaṃ mā nāmanaśānvadeśe tato gṛhyāgniṃ pratiṣṭhāpya prātarāhutiṃ hutvā vanyagotre sarvaekadeśe kṛsalīkārayet kecittriśikhāḥ kecitpañcaśikhāḥ yathāgotrakulakalpamaraṇye keśānikhaneyuḥ taṃvinidadhatyeke māṇavakaḥ punaḥ snātvā yajamānaḥ svasthānamupaviśya athopariṣṭaḥ maṃ samāpya vāmadevyaṃ gītvā tato brāhmaṇabhojanaṃ tato brāhmaṇabhojanam |
14.d: तृतीये वर्षे वपनं कार्यम् आभ्युदायिकं पूर्वे ऽह्नि ततः परे ऽहन्युषसि स्नात्वा यजमानः चतुरस्रं स्थण्डिलमुपलिष्य मण्डलाद्बहिर्दक्षिणेनाऽज्याग्नेयादि स्थापयित्वा नापितः प्राङ्मुखोपविश्य ततोष्णोपयात्रामादर्शे तदन्वन्तरं भात्कचं तत् पश्मिमेन दर्भं पिञ्जूली श्थण्डिलस्योत्तरे वायव्यादि स्नापयित्वा रक्तानडुगोमयं लौकिकत्वं कृसरस्थालीपाको वृथापक्व इति होमं मा नामनशान्वदेशे ततो गृह्याग्निं प्रतिष्ठाप्य प्रातराहुतिं हुत्वा वन्यगोत्रे सर्वएकदेशे कृसलीकारयेत् केचित्त्रिशिखाः केचित्पञ्चशिखाः यथागोत्रकुलकल्पमरण्ये केशानिखनेयुः तंविनिदधत्येके माणवकः पुनः स्नात्वा यजमानः स्वस्थानमुपविश्य अथोपरिष्टः मं समाप्य वामदेव्यं गीत्वा ततो ब्राह्मणभोजनं ततो ब्राह्मणभोजनम् ।
14.m: In the third year tonsure should be performed. The ancestral offering for prosperity is on the preceding day. Then, on the following day, having bathed at dawn, the patron of the sacrifice smears a square sacrificial ground. Having placed [the fire etc.] beginning with the fire for clarified butter to the south outside the circle, the barber sits facing east. Then a vessel with warm water and a mirror; immediately following that, a receptacle for hair; to the west of that, a bundle of darbha grass; to the north, [or] north-west, etc., of the sacrificial ground, having bathed [the boy]; fresh dung of a red bull, common [substances]; a pot-cooked offering of kṛsara, [or] what is cooked for ordinary food, saying: ‘Let there not be a sacrifice in an unfit place.’ Then, having established the domestic fire and offered the morning oblation, in a clan other than his own, in one place he should have a line made [with hair-cutting]. Some [have] three tufts of hair, some five tufts of hair, according to the rule of their clan and family. They should bury the hair in the wilderness; some dispose of it [otherwise]. The young boy having bathed again, the patron of the sacrifice sits down in his own place. Then, having completed the later [rites] and sung the Vāmadevya chant, then the feeding of brahmins; then the feeding of brahmins.

15.s: aṣṭame varṣe brahmacaryam dvādaśasaṃvatsarādarvāgā tatrāṣṭame varṣe kuryāt smṛtyukte śubhanakṣatre tasminnahani pūrvāhṇe upakramya pūrvaṃ nāndīmukaṃ kṛtvā tataḥ puṇyāhe pūrvāhṇe upakramya pūrvanāntīmukhaṃ kṛtvā tataḥ puṇyāhe pūrvāhne ācāryaḥ sahasirasaṃ snāpayitvā vaṭoḥ sarvapanaṃ kārayitvā snātvālaṃkṛtyāhatena vāsasā paridhāya caturasraṃ sthaṇḍilamupalipya prāṅmukhopaviśya pādau kṣolanīmākramya dakṣiṇe śiṣyastadvadācārya svayaṃ dārorvā dadyāttūṣṇīṃ navopataṃ vratimuce tadvaddhiraṇye lomnā carmaṇi upavītobhūtvā tayoḥ punarācamya gṛhyāgniṃ pratiṣṭhāya vismṛtaṃ sagotrer'dhaṃ caulopanayanagodāneṣu tataḥsamūhanādi prapadāntaṃ kṛtvā idhmāṅgaṃ hutvā tato 'nvārabdhāyāṃ vyāhṛtibhiḥ tisṛbhiḥ hutvā ubhābhyāṃ hastābhyāṃ māṇavakaṃ gṛhītvā yamamā dabha vācayitvā prekṣetsavitāraṃ dhyāyan nuṣṇenetyuṣṇodakaṃ prokṣedvāyuṃ dhyāyan dakṣiṇena añjaliṃ māṇavakaḥ pūrayitvā dakṣiṇataḥ keśānvāpayitvāpa undantu iti vāpayitvā viṣṇordaṣṭro 'si ityādarśa prekṣed oṣadhe trāyasvainamiti darbha piñjūlī prakṣālyā sthāne pratiṣṭhāpya svadhite nainaṃ hiṃsīḥ ityādarśaṃ oṣadhīriti saṃjojya yena pūṣeti viprāstaṃ prokṣeyuḥ anyapuruṣaḥ sakṛdāyasena pracchidyā saptabhiḥ keśāgrān darbhāgrayuktān
