15.d: अष्टमे वर्षे ब्रह्मचर्यम् द्वादशसंवत्सरादर्वागा तत्राष्टमे वर्षे कुर्यात् स्मृत्युक्ते शुभनक्षत्रे तस्मिन्नहनि पूर्वाह्णे उपक्रम्य पूर्वं नान्दीमुकं कृत्वा ततः पुण्याहे पूर्वाह्णे उपक्रम्य पूर्वनान्तीमुखं कृत्वा ततः पुण्याहे पूर्वाह्ने आचार्यः सहसिरसं स्नापयित्वा वटोः सर्वपनं कारयित्वा स्नात्वालंकृत्याहतेन वाससा परिधाय चतुरस्रं स्थण्डिलमुपलिप्य प्राङ्मुखोपविश्य पादौ क्षोलनीमाक्रम्य दक्षिणे शिष्यस्तद्वदाचार्य स्वयं दारोर्वा दद्यात्तूष्णीं नवोपतं व्रतिमुचे तद्वद्धिरण्ये लोम्ना चर्मणि उपवीतोभूत्वा तयोः पुनराचम्य गृह्याग्निं प्रतिष्ठाय विस्मृतं सगोत्रेर्ऽधं चौलोपनयनगोदानेषु ततःसमूहनादि प्रपदान्तं कृत्वा इध्माङ्गं हुत्वा ततो ऽन्वारब्धायां व्याहृतिभिः तिसृभिः हुत्वा उभाभ्यां हस्ताभ्यां माणवकं गृहीत्वा यममा दभ वाचयित्वा प्रेक्षेत्सवितारं ध्यायन् नुष्णेनेत्युष्णोदकं प्रोक्षेद्वायुं ध्यायन् दक्षिणेन अञ्जलिं माणवकः पूरयित्वा दक्षिणतः केशान्वापयित्वाप उन्दन्तु इति वापयित्वा विष्णोर्दष्ट्रो ऽसि इत्यादर्श प्रेक्षेद् ओषधे त्रायस्वैनमिति दर्भ पिञ्जूली प्रक्षाल्या स्थाने प्रतिष्ठाप्य स्वधिते नैनं हिंसीः इत्यादर्शं ओषधीरिति संजोज्य येन पूषेति विप्रास्तं प्रोक्षेयुः अन्यपुरुषः सकृदायसेन प्रच्छिद्या सप्तभिः केशाग्रान् दर्भाग्रयुक्तान् तूष्णीं अनडुह प्रक्षिप्यपुनश्च उन्दनादि प्रभृत्य एवं पश्चादुत्तरस्य त्रियायुर्षमिति मूर्धानं परिगृह्या जपे तदुपसृप्य कुर्येति ब्राह्मणं ब्रूयात् को नामेति पृच्छेदाचार्यः शिष्यो नक्षत्र स्वयं नाम ब्रूयात् तूष्णीं शिष्याञ्जलौ निलीय तथा भूमौशिष्यः ततः आचार्यो ब्रूयात् ताभ्यां हस्ताभ्यां माणवकाञ्जलिं गृह्णीयात् देवस्य त्वेत्याचार्यो मन्त्री सूर्यस्येव दुकृदात्वानावर्त्यः प्राङ्मुखस्तिष्ठन् आचार्यपृष्ठतः प्राङ्मुखः स्थित्वा उभौ करतलेन शिष्यस्य नाभिदेशं स्पृष्ट्वा प्राणानामित्य् अन्तं क इत्यदरअहुर इत्युरसि कृसर इति कण्ठे सं........... सव्येन सव्यं देवाय त्वेत्यपसव्ये वा सव्यं प्रजापतये त्वेति पुनश्च वटुः प्राङ्मुखो भूत्वाचार्यो ब्रह्मचार्योस्यसौ समिधमा धेहि आपो ऽशान कर्म कुरु मा दिवा स्वाप्सीः इति त्वं ब्रह्मचारोत्यर्थः स्वमग्नि कार्यं कुरुत स्रावमन प्राणाग्निगोत्रोदिति वा जठरत्वामित्य एवं कर्तव्यमित्याचार्यो ब्रूयातु तथास्त्विति तान् प्रतिप्य प्रातराहुतिं हुत्वा स्वसूक्तं गीत्वा प्राणायामं कुर्यात स्वगोत्रे वान्यगोत्रे वा स्वगोत्रे वेदर्यभागं दद्यादन्यगोत्रे वेत्यादं विभस्य स्वगोत्रे पुरस्ताद्देशेद एकदेशे शाउदमित्युक्त्वा प्रणयनं विदुस् तमग्निं बर्हिषि सद्यो निधाय ततः समूहनादि प्रपदान्तं कृत्वा इध्माङ्गं हुत्वा ततोन्वारब्धे व्याहृतिभिस्तिसृभिः हुत्वा पुनश्च समस्ताभिश्च हुत्वाग्ने व्रतपत इत्यादिभिः माणवको हुत्वा तत्राग्निगुर्वोमध्यनयेद् तथा मत्वा ब्राह्मण आचार्य तिष्टस्वदुः प्राङ्मुखो भूत्वा प्रागग्रान्दर्भान् ब्राह्मणं स्थित्वा पूरयित्वोदकजशं गृह्णोयात् शिष्याञ्जलिं कारयित्वा आचार्ये पर्यञ्जलिं ब्राह्मणं पूरयित्वा मन्त्रेत्याचार्ये जपित्वा शिष्याञ्जलिं प्रेक्षयेत् ब्रह्मचार्यतः प्राणायामं कृत्वा परिषिचाभ्यर्च्य अग्नये समिधमित्येकां समिधमादद्यात् प्रजापतिं मनसा द्वितीयेन हुत्वा श्रद्धा मे धेत्यग्निमुण्स्थायामात्मानमभिवाद्य त्रियायुषमिति भस्म गृहीत्वा मध्यमेलचानामिकाङ्गुष्ठेन संयूय ब्रह्मा बिन्दुरसीति भाले आयुः बिन्दुरसीति शिरसि श्रीर्बिन्दुरसीति उरसि श्रद्ध बिन्दुरसीति गले मेधा बिन्दुरसीति नाभौ तेजो बिन्दुरसीति दक्षिणबाहुमूले कामबिन्दुरसीति सव्ये वासुपृष्ठे सर्वकामेति सर्वाङ्गे वा ततो भैक्षं याचेत् तत् भैक्षं ब्रह्मणे दद्यात् आचार्याधीनः तूष्णीं तिष्ठेत् ततो मध्याङ्गे यथोक्तमार्जनं कुर्यात् सायमग्निकार्यं ततो ब्राह्मणभोजनं ततो ब्राह्मणभोजनम् ।
15.m: In the eighth year is studentship; before the twelfth year, [or] in the eighth year he should perform it, under an auspicious constellation mentioned in the Smṛti. On that day, having undertaken [the rite] in the forenoon and having first performed the ancestral offering for prosperity; then, on an auspicious day having undertaken [the rite] in the forenoon and having first performed the ancestral offering for prosperity; then, on an auspicious day in the forenoon, the preceptor, having bathed [the boy] along with his head and had a complete shaving done of the young initiate, having bathed, decorated himself, and put on an unwashed garment, smears a square sacrificial ground and sits facing east. Stepping onto the foot-washing platform, the student does likewise to the right; the preceptor himself, or of wood, should silently give a new thread [and] wrap it on him. In the same manner with gold, with the hairy hide, having put on the sacred thread, the two having sipped water again, having established the domestic fire […] in the tonsure, initiation, and the shaving of the beard. Then, having performed from the sweeping [of the hearth] up to the introductory formula, having offered the limb of firewood, then, while [the boy] holds on from behind, having offered with the three mystic utterances, taking the young boy with both hands, having made him recite […], he should look [at him] meditating on Savitṛ. With [the formula], ‘With warm [water]...’, he should sprinkle warm water, meditating on Vāyu. The young boy having filled the cavity of his hands with his right hand, having had the hair shaved on the right side, having had it shaved with [the formula], ‘May the waters moisten...’, he should look at the mirror with [the formula], ‘You are the tusk of Viṣṇu.’ Having washed the bundle of darbha grass with [the formula], ‘O herb, protect him!’, and having placed it in its spot, with [the formula], ‘Axe, do not harm him!’, joining the mirror and the herbs, the brahmins should sprinkle him with [the verse], ‘With which Pūṣan...’ Another man, having cut off the tips of the hair once with an iron [razor] along with the tips of the darbha grass, silently throws them into bull’s [dung]; and again, beginning with the moistening and so forth, in this manner on the back and on the north. Having seized his head with [the formula], ‘A life of three lifetimes...’, he should mutter. Approaching him, he should say to the brahmin: ‘Perform [it]!’ The preceptor should ask: ‘What is your name?’ The student should himself say his asterism name. Silently, into the student’s joined hands, and so on the ground, the student [pours water]. Then the preceptor should speak. With both hands he should take the young boy’s joined hands. With [the formula], ‘At the impulse of the god...’, the preceptor reciting the mantra, turning around as if toward the sun, standing facing east; standing behind the preceptor facing east, touching the student’s navel region with both palms: up to [the formula ending with] ‘... of the vital breaths.’ With [the formula], ‘Who...’, [touching] the heart; with ‘kṛsara’, the throat; […] left with left, with [the formula], ‘To the god you...’; or on the opposite side, the left [with], ‘To Prajāpati you...’ And again, the young initiate facing east, the preceptor [says]: ‘You are a Vedic student, [Name]! Add firewood! Sip water! Do your duty! Do not sleep during the day!’ That is, you are a Vedic student. ‘Perform your fire-rite! [...]’ Thus the preceptor should say: ‘It should be done.’ Having replied, ‘Let it be so!’, and having offered the morning oblation, having sung his own hymn, he should perform breath-control. In his own clan or in another clan: in his own clan he should give the portion of the Veda; or in another clan, having divided it, in his own clan in the eastern region, in one region having said ‘...’, they know it to be the bringing forward [of fire]. Having placed that fire directly on the sacrificial grass, then having performed from the sweeping up to the introductory formula, having offered the limb of firewood, then, while [the boy] holds on from behind, having offered with the three mystic utterances, and again having offered with [all of them] combined, the young boy having offered with [the verses] beginning with ‘O Agni, lord of vows...’, he should then lead him between the fire and the teacher. Considering it thus, the brahmin preceptor standing, facing east, placing darbha grass with tips pointing east, the brahmin standing, having filled and taken the water vessel, having made the student join his hands, the brahmin having filled around the hands of the preceptor, the preceptor having muttered the mantra, he should make him look at the student’s joined hands. Then, the Vedic student, having performed breath-control, having sprinkled around and worshipped, should take one piece of firewood with [the formula], ‘To Agni [I offer] the kindling stick...’ Having offered a second [stick] mentally to Prajāpati, having revered the fire with [the formula], ‘Faith and wisdom...’, having introduced himself, having taken ashes with [the formula], ‘A life of three lifetimes...’, joining them with the middle, ring finger, and thumb: on the forehead with [the formula], ‘You are the drop of Brahmā’; on the head with ‘You are the drop of life’; on the chest with ‘You are the drop of prosperity’; on the throat with ‘You are the drop of faith’; on the navel with ‘You are the drop of intellect’; at the root of the right arm with ‘You are the drop of splendour’; on the left or on the back with ‘You are the drop of desire’; or on all limbs with ‘You are all desires.’ Then he should beg for alms. He should give those alms to the Brahmā priest. Dependent on the preceptor, he should remain silent. Then he should perform the wiping as prescribed on the middle limb. In the evening is the fire-rite. Then the feeding of brahmins; then the feeding of brahmins.

16.s: atha godānabhṛtyaṃ brūyād ācāryassvasthānamupaviśya tathā brāhmaṇorbrahmāgnyormadhye māṇavakodagreṣu ca darbheṣvācāryānugo bhūtvā dakṣiṇajānvaktamupaviśyācāryo mekhalāṃ trirāvṛttāṃ badhvā māṇavako mantraṃ vāyacitvā iyaṃ duriktādityācāryaḥ punarācamya tato māṇavakaḥ suparṇavasubhāsalo bhūtvā śobhane muhūrtenvāvīhanaṃ parasparamupanayana ācāryapa asau māṇavako upaviśya tatopariṣṭāddhomaṃ samāpya tatassāvitropradānaṃ madhyaiḥ praṇavamuñcārya tataḥ pāde pāde 'vasāya tathā dvitīye 'vasāya mukhyaṃ tṛtīye tataḥ praṇavapūrvaṃ vyāhṛtīḥ pratyekamavadhāpya omityuccaiḥ tataḥ pālāśadaṇḍaṃ dadyāt suśravaḥ suśravasaṃ metyācāryojapitvā ekamahe suśravaḥ suśravasamiti māṇavakaṃ pratigrāhya tato dakṣiṇakare dve samidho gṛhṇīyāt dharmā bhavati dharmā bhavati |
16.d: अथ गोदानभृत्यं ब्रूयाद् आचार्यस्स्वस्थानमुपविश्य तथा ब्राह्मणोर्ब्रह्माग्न्योर्मध्ये माणवकोदग्रेषु च दर्भेष्वाचार्यानुगो भूत्वा दक्षिणजान्वक्तमुपविश्याचार्यो मेखलां त्रिरावृत्तां बध्वा माणवको मन्त्रं वायचित्वा इयं दुरिक्तादित्याचार्यः पुनराचम्य ततो माणवकः सुपर्णवसुभासलो भूत्वा शोभने मुहूर्तेन्वावीहनं परस्परमुपनयन आचार्यप असौ माणवको उपविश्य ततोपरिष्टाद्धोमं समाप्य ततस्सावित्रोप्रदानं मध्यैः प्रणवमुञ्चार्य ततः पादे पादे ऽवसाय तथा द्वितीये ऽवसाय मुख्यं तृतीये ततः प्रणवपूर्वं व्याहृतीः प्रत्येकमवधाप्य ओमित्युच्चैः ततः पालाशदण्डं दद्यात् सुश्रवः सुश्रवसं मेत्याचार्योजपित्वा एकमहे सुश्रवः सुश्रवसमिति माणवकं प्रतिग्राह्य ततो दक्षिणकरे द्वे समिधो गृह्णीयात् धर्मा भवति धर्मा भवति ।
16.m: Now, he should tell the attendant about the gift of cows. The preceptor, having sat down in his own place, likewise the brahmin priest between the Brahmā and the fire, and the young boy, facing north on darbha grass, following after the preceptor and sitting touching his right knee; the preceptor having tied the girdle wrapped thrice, having caused the young boy to recite the mantra: “This […] from evil speech…”; the preceptor, having sipped water again, then the young boy, becoming bright-winged and radiant in the auspicious hour, during the initiation rite mutual [...], the preceptor sitting [and] that young boy sitting, then having completed the offering of oblations (upariṣṭāddhoma), then the imparting of the Sāvitrī verse: reciting the praṇava with the middle [tones], then pausing at each quarter-verse, likewise pausing at the second, the principal [quarter] at the third; then having him insert the mystic utterances preceded by the praṇava individually, loudly uttering “Oṃ”; then he should give a staff of palāśa wood; the preceptor having muttered: “O glorious one, me glorious…”; causing the young boy to receive it with: “To the glorious one, make me glorious…”; then he should take two kindling sticks in his right hand. It becomes righteous; it becomes righteous.

17.s: athātaḥ prāyaścittānāṃ gṛhastho brahmacāro surāpānacaṇḍālābhigamanaṃ gurutalpakabrahmahatyāgovadhaṃ suvarṇasteyaṃ duṣpratigrahaṃ parānnaṃ vainalaghutvārthe brāhmaṇasya hittīrthaṃ prāyaścittaṃ vakṣyāmīti trirātramupavāsaḥ samidhaḥ śrapayitvā tato vapanaṃ kārayitvā kamaṇgalunodakaṃ gṛhītvā saritaḥ snāpayitvā kṛṣṇagomayaṃ gṛhītvā gohṛdaye jāta sthitā bhuvanaṃ pāvanīkṛte tasmātapāvanībhūtaḥ sarvapāpakṣayaṃ kurvityanena gomayaṃ gṛhītvā adbhiḥ saṃyūya pālāśaparṇaṃ gṛhītvā dvādaśasagṛhītaṃ pūrayitvā praṇamavaśatenābhimantrya mastake 'nulipya brahmasāgniparyantaṃ homatrayaṃ sarvatrābhyastatadupahṛtapāvana pūrvavat punarabhyāsa iti vā brahmacāryamadyapānamadhuprāśanam pratyarātraṃ muktyahīna iti nopavīta digambaraṃ dvārapālanaṃ kramukṣaṇaṃ divāmaithunaṃ divā punarbhojanaṃ caṇḍālasaṃbhāṣaṇamanyatṛtamanyocchiṣṭabhojanaṃ pārvaṇaprāśanaṃ sapiṇḍīmahaikoddiṣṭaṃ teṣu punarbrahmacaryaṃ kṛtsnatvāt pramādālaghutvamiti jñāyate dharmakterna kuryāt tadabhāśvamāśrayaṅgam vitatho bhavati tasmāddharmaparo nityakusumagranthābhyāsam tathā bhūtvā tayo punarācamayay prapadāntaṃ kṛtvā idhmāṅgaṃ hutvā tato 'nvābdhāyāṃ vyāhṛtibhistisṛbhiḥ hutvāgne vratādi paṃcabhirā cāryo juhuyāt śiṣyo mantraṃ vāyayitvācāryaḥ svasthāne tiṣṭhan yuvā śiṣyaḥ prāṅmukha udbhāvaṃ jalaṃ kārayitvā pitāñjaliṃ brahma pūrayitvā ācārya ā gantre mantramutkā śiṣyāḍjaliṃ prekṣet ko nāmetyācāryo manasā pṛcchet śiṣyayo nakṣatrāśrayaṃ nāma ityupāṃśasu tayoḥ svasthānamupaviśya tatopariṣṭāddhomaṃ samāpya sāvitropradānārthe tatsaviturvṛṇīmahe sūryo devasya dhīmahi bhāno so 'haṃ saṃpracodayāt iti tūṣṇī pālāśadaṇḍaṃ dadyāt tato brāhmaṇabhojanaṃ tato brāhmaṇabhojanam |
17.d: अथातः प्रायश्चित्तानां गृहस्थो ब्रह्मचारो सुरापानचण्डालाभिगमनं गुरुतल्पकब्रह्महत्यागोवधं सुवर्णस्तेयं दुष्प्रतिग्रहं परान्नं वैनलघुत्वार्थे ब्राह्मणस्य हित्तीर्थं प्रायश्चित्तं वक्ष्यामीति त्रिरात्रमुपवासः समिधः श्रपयित्वा ततो वपनं कारयित्वा कमण्गलुनोदकं गृहीत्वा सरितः स्नापयित्वा कृष्णगोमयं गृहीत्वा गोहृदये जात स्थिता भुवनं पावनीकृते तस्मातपावनीभूतः सर्वपापक्षयं कुर्वित्यनेन गोमयं गृहीत्वा अद्भिः संयूय पालाशपर्णं गृहीत्वा द्वादशसगृहीतं पूरयित्वा प्रणमवशतेनाभिमन्त्र्य मस्तके ऽनुलिप्य ब्रह्मसाग्निपर्यन्तं होमत्रयं सर्वत्राभ्यस्ततदुपहृतपावन पूर्ववत् पुनरभ्यास इति वा ब्रह्मचार्यमद्यपानमधुप्राशनम् प्रत्यरात्रं मुक्त्यहीन इति नोपवीत दिगम्बरं द्वारपालनं क्रमुक्षणं दिवामैथुनं दिवा पुनर्भोजनं चण्डालसंभाषणमन्यतृतमन्योच्छिष्टभोजनं पार्वणप्राशनं सपिण्डीमहैकोद्दिष्टं तेषु पुनर्ब्रह्मचर्यं कृत्स्नत्वात् प्रमादालघुत्वमिति ज्ञायते धर्मक्तेर्न कुर्यात् तदभाश्वमाश्रयङ्गम् वितथो भवति तस्माद्धर्मपरो नित्यकुसुमग्रन्थाभ्यासम् तथा भूत्वा तयो पुनराचमयय् प्रपदान्तं कृत्वा इध्माङ्गं हुत्वा ततो ऽन्वाब्धायां व्याहृतिभिस्तिसृभिः हुत्वाग्ने व्रतादि पंचभिरा चार्यो जुहुयात् शिष्यो मन्त्रं वाययित्वाचार्यः स्वस्थाने तिष्ठन् युवा शिष्यः प्राङ्मुख उद्भावं जलं कारयित्वा पिताञ्जलिं ब्रह्म पूरयित्वा आचार्य आ गन्त्रे मन्त्रमुत्का शिष्याड्जलिं प्रेक्षेत् को नामेत्याचार्यो मनसा पृच्छेत् शिष्ययो नक्षत्राश्रयं नाम इत्युपांशसु तयोः स्वस्थानमुपविश्य ततोपरिष्टाद्धोमं समाप्य सावित्रोप्रदानार्थे तत्सवितुर्वृणीमहे सूर्यो देवस्य धीमहि भानो सो ऽहं संप्रचोदयात् इति तूष्णी पालाशदण्डं दद्यात् ततो ब्राह्मणभोजनं ततो ब्राह्मणभोजनम् ।
17.m: Now therefore, concerning the expiations: whether householder or Vedic student, [for] drinking liquor, approaching a Caṇḍāla woman, violating the teacher's bed, killing a brahmin, slaughtering a cow, stealing gold, accepting an improper gift, [or eating] another's food—for the purpose of lightness of transgression and for the benefit of the brahmin priest, I shall declare the expiation. A fast of three nights [is observed]. Having boiled [food] on kindling sticks, then having caused tonsure to be performed, having taken water with a water pot, having bathed in a river, having taken black cow dung with [the formula]: “Born in the heart of the cow, stationed, having purified the world, therefore become purifying, destroy all sins!”, having gathered the cow dung, having mixed it with water, having taken a palāśa leaf, having filled it twelve times with what was gathered, having consecrated it with a hundred syllables of om (praṇava), having smeared it on the head, [offering] the three oblations ending with Brahmā and Agni everywhere as practiced—that brought-about purification is repeated as before. Or else, if a Vedic student [commits] the drinking of liquor, consuming honey, every night without release, without the sacred thread, going naked, guarding a door, chewing betel nut, day-time intercourse, eating again during the day, conversing with a Caṇḍāla, untruth, eating another’s leftovers, eating at a joint day (parvan) rite, an ancestral rite with food portions (sapiṇḍīkaraṇa), or a rite for a single ancestor (ekoddiṣṭa)—in those cases resumption of studentship [is prescribed] because of completeness; because of negligence it is known to be a slight offense. One should not act [contrary] to dharma; the bodily resort fails without it; therefore devoted to dharma, constantly reciting flower-like texts, having become thus, both of them having sipped water again, having performed up to the introductory formula (prapada), having offered the limb of the firewood, then while [the boy] holds on from behind, having offered with the three mystic utterances (vyāhṛtis), the preceptor should offer five [oblations] beginning with “Agne vrata...”. Having caused the student to recite the mantra, the preceptor standing in his own place, the young student facing east, having caused the water to surge up, having filled the hollow of the hands with sacred water, the preceptor having spoken the mantra to the one approaching, should look into the student’s joined palms. “What is your name?” the preceptor asks mentally. The student [answers] in a whisper: “The name connected with the asterism (nakṣatra).” Both having sat in their own places, then having completed the offering above, for the sake of imparting the Sāvitrī [verse]: “We choose that desirable [splendor] of Savitṛ; we meditate upon [the splendor] of the sun-god; may he inspire my thought”, he should silently give the palāśa staff. Then the feeding of brahmins; then the feeding of brahmins.

18.s: abhibhātmānaḥ sarvāṅgaiḥ pratyekasahasraṃ sthaṇḍilamupalipya ikṣudaṇjaśakaṃ kṛtvodagagramāstīryopari śiṣyopaveśanam navaśūrpaṃ śirasi nidhāya kuśaiḥ chādayitvācāryo ghaṭenāñjaliṃ pūrayitvā dakṣiṇapādenākramya yena deveti namantriya eto nvindretyabhiṣicya punaśca vāsasā paridhāya caturasraṃ sthaṇḍilamupalipya pūrvopanayanavat pravaṇaṃ kṛtvā brīhīn vā yavān vā yathācchakasthaṃḍilaṃ pūrayitvā taṃ śūrpaṃ tadupari nidhāya tathā śiṣyopaveśanaṃ pūrvoktamantreṇa payasādi śiṣyamastake 'bhiṣiñcet caturasraṃ sthaṇḍilamupalipya pūrvopayanavat praṇayanaṃ kṛtvācāryo mekhalāṃ trirāvṛttāṃ baddhvā tūṣṇīṃ śiṣyo mantraṃ vācayitvā yathoktamantreṇa yajñopavītī śarāvaṃ mārjayitvā śanno devīriti pañcaśataṃ yaḥ pāvamānīriti triḥ śataṃ eto nvindramaṣṭacatvāri samāṃ yatra śataṃ vā śatavāraṇapraṇavaṃ śatamaṣṭottaraṃ ebhirmārjayitvā punaśca yathoktamārjanaṃ kṛtvā śucau deśe sthaṇḍilaṃ vartayitvā vā kuśagrān sahasramādāya dviśatādhikaṃ vā śataṃ vibhajya śatāgraṃ śirasi nidhāya śataṃ pādatale nidhāyākramya pārśvayoḥ śataṃ śataṃ badhnīyāt urasi āpo hiṣṭheti sahasraṃ japitvā śanno devīriti dviguṇameto nvindraṃ catvāriṃśad gāyatraṃ pañcasahasraṃ praṇavamayutaṃ kṛtvā |
18.d: अभिभात्मानः सर्वाङ्गैः प्रत्येकसहस्रं स्थण्डिलमुपलिप्य इक्षुदण्जशकं कृत्वोदगग्रमास्तीर्योपरि शिष्योपवेशनम् नवशूर्पं शिरसि निधाय कुशैः छादयित्वाचार्यो घटेनाञ्जलिं पूरयित्वा दक्षिणपादेनाक्रम्य येन देवेति नमन्त्रिय एतो न्विन्द्रेत्यभिषिच्य पुनश्च वाससा परिधाय चतुरस्रं स्थण्डिलमुपलिप्य पूर्वोपनयनवत् प्रवणं कृत्वा ब्रीहीन् वा यवान् वा यथाच्छकस्थंडिलं पूरयित्वा तं शूर्पं तदुपरि निधाय तथा शिष्योपवेशनं पूर्वोक्तमन्त्रेण पयसादि शिष्यमस्तके ऽभिषिञ्चेत् चतुरस्रं स्थण्डिलमुपलिप्य पूर्वोपयनवत् प्रणयनं कृत्वाचार्यो मेखलां त्रिरावृत्तां बद्ध्वा तूष्णीं शिष्यो मन्त्रं वाचयित्वा यथोक्तमन्त्रेण यज्ञोपवीती शरावं मार्जयित्वा शन्नो देवीरिति पञ्चशतं यः पावमानीरिति त्रिः शतं एतो न्विन्द्रमष्टचत्वारि समां यत्र शतं वा शतवारणप्रणवं शतमष्टोत्तरं एभिर्मार्जयित्वा पुनश्च यथोक्तमार्जनं कृत्वा शुचौ देशे स्थण्डिलं वर्तयित्वा वा कुशग्रान् सहस्रमादाय द्विशताधिकं वा शतं विभज्य शताग्रं शिरसि निधाय शतं पादतले निधायाक्रम्य पार्श्वयोः शतं शतं बध्नीयात् उरसि आपो हिष्ठेति सहस्रं जपित्वा शन्नो देवीरिति द्विगुणमेतो न्विन्द्रं चत्वारिंशद् गायत्रं पञ्चसहस्रं प्रणवमयुतं कृत्वा ।
18.m: Having smeared the sacrificial ground individually a thousand times for all the limbs, having made a piece of sugarcane, having spread [darbha] with the tips pointing northward, the seating of the student upon it [takes place]. Having placed a new winnowing-basket on the head and covered it with kuśa grass, the preceptor, having filled the folded hands with a pot, having stepped forward with the right foot, consecrating with “Yena devāḥ...”, having sprinkled him with “Eto nv indram...”, and having clothed him with a garment, having smeared the square sacrificial ground, having made an incline as in the previous investiture (upanayana), having filled the ground according to desire with either rice or barley, having placed that winnowing-basket upon it, the seating of the student [takes place] likewise; he should sprinkle with milk and so forth onto the head of the student with the previously mentioned mantra. Having smeared the square sacrificial ground and performed the bringing forward [of fire] as in the previous investiture, the preceptor, having tied the girdle wound thrice, silently having the student recite the mantra, wearing the sacred thread, having wiped the shallow dish with the prescribed mantra, having wiped with “Śaṃ no devīḥ...” five hundred times, “Yaḥ pāvamānīḥ...” three hundred times, “Eto nv indram...” forty-[eight] times, where there are a hundred, or a hundred repetitions of om, one hundred and eight times, and having again performed the wiping as prescribed, having laid out the sacrificial ground in a clean place, or having taken a thousand tips of kuśa grass, or having divided a hundred into [bunches] exceeding two hundred, having placed a hundred tips on the head, having placed a hundred under the soles of the feet and stepped on them, he should tie a hundred to each of the two sides; on the chest, having muttered “Āpo hi ṣṭhā...” a thousand times, “Śaṃ no devīḥ...” twice that amount, “Eto nv indram...” forty times, the Gāyatrī five thousand times, having performed the syllable om ten thousand times.

19.s: atho opāsanavidhiṃ vyākhyāsyāmaḥ | kālo 'nādeśe sāyāmāhutyupakramya prātaḥ praste tejaḥ prāptisāyamāhur yadi samasya kṛtatvāt aprāptitvāt prātadāhuḥ so 'yaṃ yāmatrāyadarvāk yathāprāptiriti tasmātsakālaprāptirbhavati divā yāmādadvāgyathoktamiti dātistasmādaprāptirbhavati pralapya māṇavakamantraṃ punargṛhotaṃ sakṛtpraṇavenābhimantrya pītvācamyāṅgulamātraṃ jalamavagāhya prāṇāyāmaṃ sahasraṃ kṛtvāpo hi ṣṭheti śataṃ japitvā śanno dīvīriti dviśataṃ yaḥ pāvamānīriti triśataṃ eto nvindraṃ caturdaśa gāyatraṃ pañcadaśa praṇavasahasraṃ ityaṣṭa teṣāṃ sumanaso jatpa punarnābhimātraṃ jale sthitā prāṇayāmaśataṃ kṛtvāpo hiṣṭheti śatam |
19.d: अथो ओपासनविधिं व्याख्यास्यामः । कालो ऽनादेशे सायामाहुत्युपक्रम्य प्रातः प्रस्ते तेजः प्राप्तिसायमाहुर् यदि समस्य कृतत्वात् अप्राप्तित्वात् प्रातदाहुः सो ऽयं यामत्रायदर्वाक् यथाप्राप्तिरिति तस्मात्सकालप्राप्तिर्भवति दिवा यामादद्वाग्यथोक्तमिति दातिस्तस्मादप्राप्तिर्भवति प्रलप्य माणवकमन्त्रं पुनर्गृहोतं सकृत्प्रणवेनाभिमन्त्र्य पीत्वाचम्याङ्गुलमात्रं जलमवगाह्य प्राणायामं सहस्रं कृत्वापो हि ष्ठेति शतं जपित्वा शन्नो दीवीरिति द्विशतं यः पावमानीरिति त्रिशतं एतो न्विन्द्रं चतुर्दश गायत्रं पञ्चदश प्रणवसहस्रं इत्यष्ट तेषां सुमनसो जत्प पुनर्नाभिमात्रं जले स्थिता प्राणयामशतं कृत्वापो हिष्ठेति शतम् ।
19.m: Now we shall explain the rule for daily worship [of the fire]. / If the time is not specified, it begins with the evening oblation; in the morning, radiant energy is attained; it is called the evening oblation because the whole has been done; because it has not been attained, they call it the morning oblation. That [time] is before three watches, according to attainment; therefore there is timely attainment. During the day it is before a watch, as stated; because of gift, therefore there is non-attainment. Having uttered the student's mantra, having taken [water] again, having consecrated it once with the syllable om, having drunk and sipped water, having plunged into finger-deep water, having performed breath-control a thousand times, having muttered “Āpo hi ṣṭhā...” a hundred times, “Śaṃ no devīḥ...” two hundred times, “Yaḥ pāvamānīḥ...” three hundred times, “Eto nv indram...” fourteen times, the Gāyatrī fifteen times, a thousand syllables of om, having muttered these eight with a concentrated mind, standing again in navel-deep water, having performed a hundred breath-controls, “Āpo hi ṣṭhā...” a hundred times.

20.s: atha punarbrahmacaryavidhiṃ vyākhyāsyāmaḥ | ṣaṇmāsān payobhakṣaḥ samudramavahagāhya pūrvavannāndadīmukhaṃ kṛtvā tato vapanaṃ kārayitvā aṣṭo brahmaṇānniyojya aṣṭo mṛnmayeṣu dadhimadhvājyapayaḥ śarkarīdakaṃ nālikerajalaṃ puroṣaṃ gaṃgātoyaṃ etānpūrayitvāhatena vāsasā pariveśyā ā pyāyasveti kṣīrapātramabhimantrya dadhikrāviṇeti dadhipātraṃ śukramasasīti ghṛtapātraṃ madhaduścunnadhanamiti madhupātram āpo hi ṣṭheti śarkarām kayā naścitra iti nālikeram gāyatre gomūtraṃ evaṃ deveti ścarṇodapātramiti |
20.d: अथ पुनर्ब्रह्मचर्यविधिं व्याख्यास्यामः । षण्मासान् पयोभक्षः समुद्रमवहगाह्य पूर्ववन्नान्ददीमुखं कृत्वा ततो वपनं कारयित्वा अष्टो ब्रह्मणान्नियोज्य अष्टो मृन्मयेषु दधिमध्वाज्यपयः शर्करीदकं नालिकेरजलं पुरोषं गंगातोयं एतान्पूरयित्वाहतेन वाससा परिवेश्या आ प्यायस्वेति क्षीरपात्रमभिमन्त्र्य दधिक्राविणेति दधिपात्रं शुक्रमससीति घृतपात्रं मधदुश्चुन्नधनमिति मधुपात्रम् आपो हि ष्ठेति शर्कराम् कया नश्चित्र इति नालिकेरम् गायत्रे गोमूत्रं एवं देवेति श्चर्णोदपात्रमिति ।
20.m: Now we shall explain the rule for resumption of studentship. / For six months subsisting on milk, having bathed in the ocean, having performed the ancestral offering for prosperity (nāndīmukha) as before, then having caused tonsure to be done, having appointed eight brahmins, having filled eight earthen vessels with curd, honey, clarified butter, milk, sugar-water, coconut-water, cow dung, and Gaṅgā water, having covered them with an unwashed garment, having consecrated the milk vessel with “Ā pyāyasva...”, the curd vessel with “Dadhikrāvṇā...”, the clarified butter vessel with “Śukram asi...”, the honey vessel with “Madhu vātāḥ...”, the sugar[-water] with “Āpo hi ṣṭhā...”, the coconut[-water] with “Kayā naś citraḥ...”, cow urine with the Gāyatrī, and the pure water vessel with “Evaṃ devāḥ...”.

21.s: ityete vā vāmityuccaiḥ brūyāt pradakṣiṇena jalaṃ vīkṣyādityamādityamaśaktascet pratiyāme sakṛt ghaṭikāvasānaṃ vātāstamayād bhavati tataḥ sāya mārjayatvā kamaṇḍalunodakaṃ gṛhītvā maḍhaṃ praviśet | prāṅmukhopaviśya tata udakaṃ pītvā netrayīḥ prakṣālyācamya tataḥ prāṇāpānau dvau tavaśyāvīyau dvau rājanaśāśāhiṇābhyāṃ gavāṃ vrate dve idaṃ viṣṇuḥ ṣaḍṛcaṃ devavratāni eteṣāṃ punaḥ punarabhyāso na tiṣṭhaṃ vāvasānaṃ na nidraṃ drācaṃ iti dvādaśarātramupavāso hyāparevādvrataṃ na yācate | dvādaśarātra nāśroyāt ityevaṃ dvādaśarātramupavāsaḥ kṛtvātikṛtsna iti smṛtam | yāvadbṛhaspatirbrahmā tāvatsvarge loke mahīyate na ca punarāvartate na ca punarāvartate |
21.d: इत्येते वा वामित्युच्चैः ब्रूयात् प्रदक्षिणेन जलं वीक्ष्यादित्यमादित्यमशक्तस्चेत् प्रतियामे सकृत् घटिकावसानं वातास्तमयाद् भवति ततः साय मार्जयत्वा कमण्डलुनोदकं गृहीत्वा मढं प्रविशेत् । प्राङ्मुखोपविश्य तत उदकं पीत्वा नेत्रयीः प्रक्षाल्याचम्य ततः प्राणापानौ द्वौ तवश्यावीयौ द्वौ राजनशाशाहिणाभ्यां गवां व्रते द्वे इदं विष्णुः षडृचं देवव्रतानि एतेषां पुनः पुनरभ्यासो न तिष्ठं वावसानं न निद्रं द्राचं इति द्वादशरात्रमुपवासो ह्यापरेवाद्व्रतं न याचते । द्वादशरात्र नाश्रोयात् इत्येवं द्वादशरात्रमुपवासः कृत्वातिकृत्स्न इति स्मृतम् । यावद्बृहस्पतिर्ब्रह्मा तावत्स्वर्गे लोके महीयते न च पुनरावर्तते न च पुनरावर्तते ।
21.m:
With these [mantras] he should recite loudly, "vā vām...". Having circumambulated from left to right, looked at the water and at the sun—or if he is unable, once every watch of the day or at the end of a ghaṭikā until sunset—then in the evening, having sprinkled himself, taken water with his water pot, he should enter the cell.
Having sat down facing east, then having drunk water, washed both eyes, and sipped water, then [reciting] the two Prāṇāpāna [verses], the two Tavaśyāvīya [sāmans], the two Rājana and Śāśāhiṇa [sāmans], the two Gavāṃ vrata [sāmans], "idaṃ viṣṇuḥ", the six-verse hymn, and the Devavrata [sāmans]—the repeated recitation of these [takes place], not standing, not resting, and not sleeping. Thus a fast of twelve nights [is undertaken]; he does not ask for [anything] during the observance until the next day.
He should not eat for twelve nights; thus having performed a fast of twelve nights, it is remembered as the Atikṛtsna [penance].
For as long as Bṛhaspati and Brahmā [endure], so long is he magnified in the heavenly world; and he does not return, and he does not return.
